fundamentals/fundamentals.title: Fundamentals
fundamentals/fundamentals.summary: Welcome to the start of the road.

fundamentals/what-is-ai.title: What Is AI
fundamentals/what-is-ai.summary: This district answers the first question: what is AI? The honest answer is that the word covers a family of ideas, and which systems count depends on how you define it.

fundamentals/what-counts-as-ai.title: What Counts as AI
fundamentals/what-counts-as-ai.path: Fundamentals/What Is AI/What Counts as AI.md
fundamentals/what-counts-as-ai.summary: Artificial intelligence has no single agreed definition, so whether something "counts" depends on the question you ask.

glossary.def: the field, and the systems, aimed at machines that sense, decide and act towards goals.
Turing's imitation game, in which a judge tries to tell a machine from a person by conversation alone.
an agent that chooses the action expected to best achieve its goal, given what it knows.
the habit of no longer calling a technique AI once it has become routine.

fundamentals/ai-ml-dl-and-generative-ai.title: AI, ML, DL and Generative AI
fundamentals/ai-ml-dl-and-generative-ai.path: Fundamentals/What Is AI/AI, ML, DL and Generative AI.md
fundamentals/ai-ml-dl-and-generative-ai.summary: AI, machine learning, deep learning and generative AI are nested ideas, like Russian dolls.

glossary.def: methods in which a system learns patterns from data instead of following hand-written rules.
a model built from many simple connected units whose connection strengths are learned.
machine learning with neural networks that have many layers.
models that create new content such as text, images, audio or code.

fundamentals/rules-vs-learning.title: Rules vs Learning
fundamentals/rules-vs-learning.summary: There are two ways to make a machine behave well: write the rules by hand, or show it examples and let it work the rules out. Hand-written rules are clear but brittle.

glossary.def: one whose behaviour is set by hand-written if-then rules.
the examples a system learns from.
the correct answer attached to a training example, such as “spam”.
working only in the situations it was written for, and failing badly outside them.

fundamentals/narrow-general-and-super-ai.title: Narrow, General and Super AI
fundamentals/narrow-general-and-super-ai.path: Fundamentals/What Is AI/Narrow, General and Super AI.md
fundamentals/narrow-general-and-super-ai.summary: Narrow AI does one job, or a small family of jobs, very well. General AI would handle a wide range of tasks the way a person can. Superintelligence would go far beyond human ability.

glossary.def: a system built for one task or a tight family of tasks.
a hypothetical system flexible across most intellectual tasks a person can do. There is no agreed definition or test.
a hypothetical system far better than the best humans at nearly everything.
being excellent at one task and weak at a similar-looking one.

fundamentals/a-short-history-of-ai.title: A Short History of AI
fundamentals/a-short-history-of-ai.path: Fundamentals/What Is AI/A Short History of AI.md
fundamentals/a-short-history-of-ai.summary: AI's history is a pattern of big promises, real breakthroughs, disappointment and funding cuts, then a new approach and a new wave. The two long slumps are called AI winters.

glossary.def: a period of sharply reduced funding and interest after a wave of over-promising.
an early learning model: a single artificial neuron that classifies its inputs.
a rule-based program that captures a specialist's knowledge.
the method for training multi-layer networks by passing the error backwards through them.
a neural network architecture built on attention, introduced in 2017.

fundamentals/the-agent.title: The Agent
fundamentals/the-agent.summary: Almost every AI system, however different it looks, has the same shape: it is an agent inside an environment. It senses what is happening, decides what to do to reach a goal, and acts, over and over.

fundamentals/agents-and-environments.title: Agents and Environments
fundamentals/agents-and-environments.summary: An agent is anything that perceives its surroundings through sensors and acts on them through actuators to pursue a goal. The surroundings it lives in are its environment.

glossary.def: anything that perceives its environment through sensors and acts on it through actuators to pursue a goal.
everything outside the agent that it senses and affects.
a channel through which the agent receives information: a camera, a microphone, a data feed.
a channel through which the agent acts: a motor, a screen, an outgoing message.
what the sensors report at one moment.

fundamentals/pda-loop.title: PDA Loop
fundamentals/pda-loop.summary: The Perception → Decision → Action loop is the heartbeat of every intelligent system.

glossary.def: turning raw signals into an understanding of the situation.
choosing an action based on that understanding and the goal.
carrying out the choice and changing the world.
the effect of an action coming back as the next perception.
a system that checks the results of its actions and adjusts, unlike an open loop that acts blindly.

fundamentals/goals-utility-and-rationali.title: Goals, Utility and Rationality
fundamentals/goals-utility-and-rationali.summary: An agent needs a way to choose between options.

glossary.def: what the agent is trying to achieve.
a number scoring how good an outcome is for the agent.
the average result when each possible outcome is weighted by its chance.
choosing the action with the best expected result given what is known, not necessarily the best in hindsight.
an objective that differs from what its designers actually wanted.

fundamentals/state-and-representation.title: State and Representation
fundamentals/state-and-representation.summary: The state is the agent's summary of the situation: everything it needs to know to choose a good action, and nothing more.

glossary.def: the agent's summary of the situation, holding every fact its decision depends on.
the form in which the state is written: numbers, a table, a graph or learned vectors.
the way the number of possible states multiplies with each extra fact.
a list of numbers, usually learned by a model, that represents something such as a word.

fundamentals/kinds-of-environments.title: Kinds of Environments
fundamentals/kinds-of-environments.summary: Some AI problems are easy and others are brutal, and much of the difference lies in the environment.

glossary.def: whether the agent can see everything relevant.
whether outcomes are fixed by the state and action, or involve chance.
whether decisions stand alone or shape later options.
whether the world waits for the agent or keeps changing.
an environment in which other agents also act, cooperating or competing.

fundamentals/data-and-models.title: Data and Models
fundamentals/data-and-models.summary: Before an AI system can decide anything, it has to perceive, and for most modern systems perceiving means turning the world into data.

fundamentals/data-as-raw-material.title: Data as Raw Material
fundamentals/data-as-raw-material.path: Fundamentals/Data and Models/Data as Raw Material.md
fundamentals/data-as-raw-material.summary: Data is recorded information about the world: measurements, text, images, sound, clicks, transactions.

glossary.def: recorded information about the world.
data in neat rows and columns, like a spreadsheet.
free-form data such as text, images and audio.
measurements recorded in order over time.
a chunk of text, such as a word or word piece, converted into a number.

fundamentals/features-and-labels.title: Features and Labels
fundamentals/features-and-labels.summary: Features are the measurable facts a model looks at, and a label is the answer it is asked to predict.

glossary.def: one measurable fact about an example.
the list of an example's features.
the answer the model is asked to predict.
choosing and shaping features by hand to give a model useful information.

fundamentals/a-model-is-a-function.title: A Model Is a Function
fundamentals/a-model-is-a-function.path: Fundamentals/Data and Models/A Model Is a Function.md
fundamentals/a-model-is-a-function.summary: A model is a function: give it inputs and it returns a prediction.

glossary.def: a function that turns inputs into a prediction.
an adjustable number inside a model, set by learning.
the output the model produces for an input.
a number measuring how far predictions are from the true answers.

fundamentals/training-vs-inference.title: Training vs Inference
fundamentals/training-vs-inference.summary: Training is when a model's parameters are adjusted using examples. Inference is when the finished, frozen model is used to make predictions on new inputs.

glossary.def: adjusting a model's parameters using examples.
using a trained, frozen model to make predictions on new inputs.
the number that training tries to make small.
repeatedly nudging parameters in the direction that lowers the loss.
no longer improving noticeably, so training can stop.

fundamentals/types-of-tasks.title: Types of Tasks
fundamentals/types-of-tasks.summary: Most AI problems fall into a few kinds: classify (pick a category), predict a number, group similar things without labels, generate new content, or choose actions over time.

glossary.def: predicting which category an example belongs to.
predicting a number.
grouping similar examples when no labels are given.
learning from examples that come with correct answers.
learning which actions to take from feedback about their results.

fundamentals/classic-ai.title: Classic AI
fundamentals/classic-ai.summary: Before machine learning took over, AI meant searching, reasoning and planning with hand-built knowledge.

fundamentals/search.title: Search
fundamentals/search.summary: Search is how a machine finds a path or a plan by exploring possibilities systematically.

glossary.def: all the states a problem can be in, joined by actions.
the states discovered but not yet explored.
the check that says a state is a solution.
exploring the nearest states first, in rings.
following one route as deep as possible before backing up.
the number of actions available from a typical state.

fundamentals/heuristics-and-a-star-searc.title: Heuristics and A-star Search
fundamentals/heuristics-and-a-star-searc.summary: A heuristic is an informed guess about how far you still are from the goal.

glossary.def: a cheap, informed estimate of how far a state is from the goal.
one that never overestimates the true remaining cost.
the steps needed on a grid if nothing blocked the way: |Δrow| + |Δcolumn|.
a search that follows the heuristic alone.

fundamentals/logic-and-knowledge-represe.title: Logic and Knowledge Representation
fundamentals/logic-and-knowledge-represe.summary: Classic AI stored what it knew as facts and rules, and used inference to work out new facts from them. Writing knowledge in a form a machine can reason with is called knowledge representation.

glossary.def: a statement taken to be true.
an if-then statement saying what follows from what.
deriving new facts from known facts and rules.
applying rules repeatedly to known facts until nothing new appears.
facts stored as things linked by relations.
a structured description of categories and how they relate.

fundamentals/planning.title: Planning
fundamentals/planning.summary: Planning is finding a sequence of actions that turns the current situation into a goal.

glossary.def: a sequence of actions that reaches a goal.
what must be true before an action is allowed.
what changes after an action.
making a new plan when the world does not go as expected.
an early planning language that described actions by their preconditions and effects.

fundamentals/expert-systems-and-their-li.title: Expert Systems and Their Limits
fundamentals/expert-systems-and-their-li.path: Fundamentals/Classic AI/Expert Systems and Their Limits.md
fundamentals/expert-systems-and-their-li.summary: An expert system captures the knowledge of human specialists as a set of if-then rules and applies them with an inference engine. In the 1980s they powered a commercial AI boom.

glossary.def: the collection of rules and facts written by people.
the general machinery that applies the rules to a case.
the difficulty of getting experts' skill into explicit rules.
failing badly outside the situations the rules cover.

fundamentals/judging-ai.title: Judging AI
fundamentals/judging-ai.summary: Building an AI system is only half the job. The other half is judging it: how do you know it works, whether it will keep working on new cases, and where it is likely to fail?

fundamentals/measuring-performance.title: Measuring Performance
fundamentals/measuring-performance.summary: To judge an AI system you have to count its hits, misses and false alarms, not just its overall accuracy.

glossary.def: the table of hits, misses, false alarms and correct ignores.
the share of all cases handled correctly.
the share of real cases the system catches.
the share of the system's alarms that are real.
how common the thing you are looking for is.

fundamentals/generalization.title: Generalization
fundamentals/generalization.summary: Generalization is a model's ability to do well on examples it has never seen. A model that merely memorises its training examples, noise and all, scores perfectly on them and poorly on anything new.

glossary.def: the examples a model learns from.
examples held back to judge the finished model.
fitting the quirks and noise of the training data, so new data goes badly.
being too simple to capture the real pattern.
random errors or variation in data that hides the true pattern.

fundamentals/where-ai-goes-wrong.title: Where AI Goes Wrong
fundamentals/where-ai-goes-wrong.summary: AI systems fail in patterned ways: they learn from unrepresentative or biased data, they meet a world that has changed since training, they can be brittle to tiny changes, and they can be…

glossary.def: a lopsided or unrepresentative sample that skews what a model learns.
new data differing from the data a model was trained on.
an input altered slightly, often invisibly, to make a model err.
a system's outputs changing the data it later learns from.
a fluent output that is confidently wrong or invented.

fundamentals/anatomy-of-an-ai-system.title: Anatomy of an AI System
fundamentals/anatomy-of-an-ai-system.path: Fundamentals/Judging AI/Anatomy of an AI System.md
fundamentals/anatomy-of-an-ai-system.summary: Every AI system, from a thermostat to a chatbot, can be described with the same seven parts: a goal, the data it uses, a model or rule, and a loop of perceive, decide, act, all judged by some…

glossary.def: a goal, data, a model or rule, a perceive–decide–act loop and a measure of success working together.
a number that summarises how well a system does its job.
putting a trained system into real use.
the chain of steps from raw data to a decision and an action.

math/math.title: Math
math/math.summary: Every AI model is, underneath, arithmetic done at enormous scale.

math/arithmetic-and-number-sense.title: Arithmetic and Number Sense
math/arithmetic-and-number-sense.path: Math/Arithmetic and Number Sense/Arithmetic and Number Sense.md
math/arithmetic-and-number-sense.summary: Before vectors and gradients come the numbers themselves.

math/numbers-and-their-kinds.title: Numbers and Their Kinds
math/numbers-and-their-kinds.path: Math/Arithmetic and Number Sense/Numbers and Their Kinds.md
math/numbers-and-their-kinds.summary: Numbers come in nested families: natural numbers for counting, integers that add negatives, rational numbers that are fractions, and real numbers that fill the whole number line.

glossary.def: a counting number: 1, 2, 3, …
a whole number, positive, negative or zero.
a number that can be written as a fraction of two integers.
a real number that is not rational, like √2 or π.
any point on the number line.

math/fractions-ratios-and-percentages.title: Fractions, Ratios and Percentages
math/fractions-ratios-and-percentages.path: Math/Arithmetic and Number Sense/Fractions, Ratios and Percentages.md
math/fractions-ratios-and-percentages.summary: A fraction, a decimal and a percentage are three ways of writing the same quantity, and a ratio compares two quantities.

glossary.def: a number written as a part over a whole, a/b.
a number written with digits after a point.
a share out of 100.
a comparison of two quantities, a : b.
the difference between two percentages.

math/order-of-operations-and-properties.title: Order of Operations and Properties
math/order-of-operations-and-properties.path: Math/Arithmetic and Number Sense/Order of Operations and Properties.md
math/order-of-operations-and-properties.summary: An expression such as 2 + 3 × 4 has one right answer because everyone agrees on the order of operations: parentheses first, then powers, then multiplication and division, then addition and…

glossary.def: the agreed sequence for evaluating an expression.
the order of two operands does not change the result.
regrouping does not change the result.
a(b + c) = ab + ac.

math/exponents-and-roots.title: Exponents and Roots
math/exponents-and-roots.path: Math/Arithmetic and Number Sense/Exponents and Roots.md
math/exponents-and-roots.summary: An exponent says how many times to multiply a number by itself, and a root undoes it.

glossary.def: the number of times a base is multiplied by itself.
the number being multiplied.
the number that, raised to a power, gives a target.
1/a, the number that multiplies a to give 1.

math/scientific-notation-and-scale.title: Scientific Notation and Scale
math/scientific-notation-and-scale.path: Math/Arithmetic and Number Sense/Scientific Notation and Scale.md
math/scientific-notation-and-scale.summary: Scientific notation writes a number as a digit-and-decimal part times a power of ten, so 6,000,000 becomes 6 × 10⁶ and 0.00042 becomes 4.2 × 10⁻⁴.

glossary.def: a number as a × 10ⁿ with 1 ≤ a < 10.
a factor of ten.
the same thing written aeN.
here, the power of ten that sets the scale.

math/logarithms.title: Logarithms
math/logarithms.summary: A logarithm answers "what power do I raise this base to, to get that number?" log₂ 8 = 3 because 2³ = 8.

glossary.def: the exponent needed to reach a number from a base.
the logarithm with base e ≈ 2.718.
the number being raised to a power.
converting between logarithm bases.

math/rounding-absolute-value-and-modulo.title: Rounding, Absolute Value and Modulo
math/rounding-absolute-value-and-modulo.path: Math/Arithmetic and Number Sense/Rounding, Absolute Value and Modulo.md
math/rounding-absolute-value-and-modulo.summary: Four small operations show up constantly: rounding (to the nearest whole number or a set of decimals), floor and ceiling (always down or always up), absolute value (distance from zero) and modulo…

glossary.def: replacing a number by the nearest one at a chosen precision.
the nearest integer below and above.
a number's distance from zero.
the remainder after division.

math/estimation-and-sanity-checks.title: Estimation and Sanity Checks
math/estimation-and-sanity-checks.path: Math/Arithmetic and Number Sense/Estimation and Sanity Checks.md
math/estimation-and-sanity-checks.summary: Estimation is getting an answer that is close enough, quickly, and a sanity check is asking whether an answer is even plausible.

glossary.def: an approximate answer good enough for a purpose.
a quick test of whether an answer is plausible.
the power of ten of a number.
a rough answer built from a chain of guessable pieces.

math/reading-math-notation.title: Reading Math Notation
math/reading-math-notation.path: Math/Arithmetic and Number Sense/Reading Math Notation.md
math/reading-math-notation.summary: Maths is written in a compact shorthand: Greek letters for quantities, a few symbols for operations and relations, and conventions such as subscripts and hats.

glossary.def: a character standing for a quantity, operation or relation.
a small label giving an item's position or name.
a mark such as ŷ meaning an estimate or prediction.
the sum written with Σ.

math/algebra-and-functions.title: Algebra and Functions
math/algebra-and-functions.summary: Algebra is arithmetic with unknowns, and a function is a rule that turns inputs into outputs.

math/variables-and-expressions.title: Variables and Expressions
math/variables-and-expressions.summary: A variable is a letter that stands for a number that can change or that we do not know yet, and an expression combines variables, numbers and operations into a calculation.

glossary.def: a letter standing for a number that can vary or is unknown.
numbers, variables and operations combined.
the number multiplying a variable.
replacing variables with values.

math/equations-and-solving.title: Equations and Solving
math/equations-and-solving.summary: An equation says two expressions are equal, and solving it means finding the value of the unknown that makes the statement true.

glossary.def: a statement that two expressions are equal.
a value of the unknown that makes the equation true.
the operation that undoes another.
the rule that any move must apply to each side.

math/inequalities.title: Inequalities
math/inequalities.summary: An inequality compares two expressions with <, >, ≤ or ≥, and its answer is usually a whole range of numbers rather than one.

glossary.def: a comparison using <, >, ≤ or ≥.
all values that satisfy it.
excluded (<, >) or included (≤, ≥).
the allowed size of a difference.

math/sequences-and-series.title: Sequences and Series
math/sequences-and-series.summary: A sequence is an ordered list of numbers that follows a rule, and a series is what you get by adding its terms.

glossary.def: an ordered list following a rule.
the sum of a sequence's terms.
the fixed step or factor.
a rule defining each term from earlier ones.

math/sums-and-products.title: Sums and Products
math/sums-and-products.summary: Summation (Σ) and product (Π) notation write a long repeated addition or multiplication in one short line. They are literally a loop: "for each i from a to b, add (or multiply) this in".

glossary.def: the sum of a list of terms.
the product of a list of terms.
the counter running from the lower to the upper limit.
the product 1 × 2 × … × n.

math/functions.title: Functions
math/functions.summary: A function is a rule that takes an input and gives back exactly one output.

glossary.def: a rule giving exactly one output for each allowed input.
the allowed inputs.
the outputs that occur.
a graph is a function if no vertical line crosses it twice.

math/graphs-and-transformations.title: Graphs and Transformations
math/graphs-and-transformations.summary: A graph draws a function as a curve: input along the bottom, output up the side. Transformations shift, stretch and flip that curve, and one short formula, a · f(x − h) + k, describes them all.

glossary.def: the picture of a function's inputs and outputs.
a shift, stretch or flip of a graph.
an input where the output is zero.
the tip or turning point of a curve.

math/linear-functions.title: Linear Functions
math/linear-functions.summary: A linear function y = m·x + b draws a straight line: m is its slope (how steeply it rises) and b is its intercept (where it crosses the vertical axis).

glossary.def: y = mx + b, a straight line.
the change in output per unit of input.
the output when the input is zero.
how slope is computed.

math/polynomials-and-quadratics.title: Polynomials and Quadratics
math/polynomials-and-quadratics.summary: A polynomial is a sum of powers of x with coefficients: 3x³ − 2x + 5. The simplest curved one is the quadratic, ax² + bx + c, which draws a parabola.

glossary.def: a sum of powers of x with coefficients.
a degree-2 polynomial, ax² + bx + c.
an input where the function is zero.
b² − 4ac, which counts the real roots.

math/exponential-and-logarithmic-functio.title: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions
math/exponential-and-logarithmic-functio.path: Math/Algebra and Functions/Exponential and Logarithmic Functions.md
math/exponential-and-logarithmic-functio.summary: An exponential function f(t) = a·bᵗ multiplies by the same factor every step, so it grows (or decays) faster and faster. Its inverse, the logarithmic function, grows slower and slower.

glossary.def: a·bᵗ, multiplying by a fixed factor each step.
base above 1 or between 0 and 1.
the natural base, about 2.71828.
steps to double or halve.

math/composition-and-inverses.title: Composition and Inverses
math/composition-and-inverses.summary: Composition feeds the output of one function into another: g(f(x)). An inverse undoes a function: f⁻¹(f(x)) = x.

glossary.def: applying one function after another, g(f(x)).
the function that undoes another.
each output comes from a single input.
how an inverse's graph relates to the original.

math/functions-ai-loves.title: Functions AI Loves
math/functions-ai-loves.summary: A few specific functions turn up in almost every neural network: the sigmoid, tanh, ReLU, its leaky variant and softplus.

glossary.def: a non-linear function applied inside a network.
a smooth S-curve from 0 to 1.
max(0, x).
not describable by a straight line.

math/geometry-and-trigonometry.title: Geometry and Trigonometry
math/geometry-and-trigonometry.summary: Geometry is the maths of position, distance, angle and shape.

math/coordinates-and-distance.title: Coordinates and Distance
math/coordinates-and-distance.summary: A coordinate system locates a point with numbers, (x, y) on a plane, and a distance formula measures how far apart two points are.

glossary.def: numbers locating a point.
the point (0, 0).
straight-line distance.
sum of the horizontal and vertical gaps.

math/angles-and-radians.title: Angles and Radians
math/angles-and-radians.summary: An angle measures a turn. Degrees split a full turn into 360 parts, and radians measure it by the length of the arc it cuts from a circle of radius 1, so a full turn is 2π.

glossary.def: a measure of turn.
the angle whose arc equals the radius.
1/360 of a full turn.
the length of the curve cut off by an angle.

math/sine-cosine-and-the-unit-circle.title: Sine, Cosine and the Unit Circle
math/sine-cosine-and-the-unit-circle.path: Math/Geometry and Trigonometry/Sine, Cosine and the Unit Circle.md
math/sine-cosine-and-the-unit-circle.summary: Sine and cosine turn an angle into the height and width of a point on a circle of radius 1, the unit circle.

glossary.def: the circle of radius 1 around the origin.
the height and width of a point on the unit circle.
the length after which a wave repeats.
a wave's peak height.

math/lines-planes-and-circles.title: Lines, Planes and Circles
math/lines-planes-and-circles.path: Math/Geometry and Trigonometry/Lines, Planes and Circles.md
math/lines-planes-and-circles.summary: A line, a circle and a plane are the basic shapes, and each has a short equation.

glossary.def: the basic shapes.
a direction perpendicular to a plane.
a plane in more than three dimensions.
a line that touches a curve at exactly one point.

math/areas-volumes-and-scaling.title: Areas, Volumes and Scaling
math/areas-volumes-and-scaling.path: Math/Geometry and Trigonometry/Areas, Volumes and Scaling.md
math/areas-volumes-and-scaling.summary: Area measures a flat region and volume measures a solid. When you scale a shape by a factor k, lengths grow by k, areas by k² and volumes by k³.

glossary.def: the size of a flat region.
the size of a solid.
the number by which lengths are multiplied.
the total area of a solid's outside.

math/geometry-in-many-dimensions.title: Geometry in Many Dimensions
math/geometry-in-many-dimensions.path: Math/Geometry and Trigonometry/Geometry in Many Dimensions.md
math/geometry-in-many-dimensions.summary: Data in AI often has hundreds or thousands of coordinates, so points live in spaces we cannot picture.

glossary.def: the number of coordinates describing a point.
the problems that arise as dimension grows.
distances between points becoming nearly equal.
a flat boundary in high dimensions.

math/sets-logic-and-counting.title: Sets, Logic and Counting
math/sets-logic-and-counting.path: Math/Sets, Logic and Counting/Sets, Logic and Counting.md
math/sets-logic-and-counting.summary: This district covers the discrete foundations: collections of things (sets), statements that are true or false (logic), how to argue carefully (proofs), how to count possibilities, how to describe…

math/sets-and-operations.title: Sets and Operations
math/sets-and-operations.path: Math/Sets, Logic and Counting/Sets and Operations.md
math/sets-and-operations.summary: A set is a collection of distinct things, and a few operations (union, intersection, difference, complement) combine sets.

glossary.def: a collection of distinct elements.
elements in either / in both sets.
elements not in the set.
a set contained within another.

math/logic-and-truth-tables.title: Logic and Truth Tables
math/logic-and-truth-tables.path: Math/Sets, Logic and Counting/Logic and Truth Tables.md
math/logic-and-truth-tables.summary: Logic deals with statements that are either true or false and the ways of combining them: AND, OR, NOT, XOR and IF … THEN.

glossary.def: a list of all cases and the resulting truth value.
AND, OR, NOT, XOR or IF-THEN.
having identical truth tables.
the rules for negating AND and OR.

math/reading-proofs-and-quantifiers.title: Reading Proofs and Quantifiers
math/reading-proofs-and-quantifiers.path: Math/Sets, Logic and Counting/Reading Proofs and Quantifiers.md
math/reading-proofs-and-quantifiers.summary: A proof is an argument that a statement is true in every case, built from clear steps. Quantifiers ("for all", "there exists") say how many cases a statement covers.

glossary.def: an argument showing a statement holds in every case.
∀ (for all) or ∃ (there exists).
a case that breaks a "for all" claim.
proving a claim for every whole number via a base case and a step.

math/counting-rules.title: Counting Rules
math/counting-rules.summary: Counting answers "how many ways can this happen?" without listing them all.

glossary.def: independent choices multiply.
either-or choices add.
subtracting overlaps when adding counts.
counts growing too fast to enumerate.

math/permutations-and-combinations.title: Permutations and Combinations
math/permutations-and-combinations.path: Math/Sets, Logic and Counting/Permutations and Combinations.md
math/permutations-and-combinations.summary: A permutation counts arrangements where order matters, and a combination counts selections where order does not matter.

glossary.def: the product of the numbers from 1 to n.
an ordered arrangement.
an unordered selection.
C(n, k), "n choose k".

math/graphs-and-networks.title: Graphs and Networks
math/graphs-and-networks.path: Math/Sets, Logic and Counting/Graphs and Networks.md
math/graphs-and-networks.summary: A graph is a set of nodes joined by edges. It is the natural way to describe anything connected: friends, roads, web pages, atoms, and the computation inside a neural network.

glossary.def: nodes joined by edges.
the number of edges at a node.
a route along edges.
a table showing which nodes are joined.

math/trees-and-hierarchies.title: Trees and Hierarchies
math/trees-and-hierarchies.path: Math/Sets, Logic and Counting/Trees and Hierarchies.md
math/trees-and-hierarchies.summary: A tree is a connected graph with no cycles: one root, branches, and leaves at the ends.

glossary.def: a connected graph with no cycles.
the top node / a node with no children.
the number of edges from the root.
each node has at most two children.

math/growth-rates-and-big-o.title: Growth Rates and Big-O
math/growth-rates-and-big-o.path: Math/Sets, Logic and Counting/Growth Rates and Big-O.md
math/growth-rates-and-big-o.summary: Big-O notation describes how the cost of an algorithm (time or memory) grows as the input size n grows, ignoring constant factors.

glossary.def: an upper bound on how cost grows with n.
growth like n, n² and 2ⁿ.
cost in steps and in memory.
exponential growth in the number of options.

math/linear-algebra.title: Linear Algebra
math/linear-algebra.summary: Linear algebra is the maths of lists of numbers (vectors) and grids of numbers (matrices), and of the simple operations that combine them.

math/scalars-and-vectors.title: Scalars and Vectors
math/scalars-and-vectors.summary: A scalar is a single number, and a vector is an ordered list of numbers.

glossary.def: a single number.
an ordered list of numbers.
one number in a vector.
the number of components.
the length of a vector.

math/vector-operations.title: Vector Operations
math/vector-operations.summary: Vectors can be added, subtracted and scaled, all component by component. These three moves are the foundation of everything in linear algebra: every model computation is built from them.

glossary.def: adding matching components.
multiplying every component by a number.
the arrow from one point to another.
multiplying matching components.

math/linear-combinations-and-span.title: Linear Combinations and Span
math/linear-combinations-and-span.summary: A linear combination of vectors is a sum of scaled copies: c₁v₁ + c₂v₂ + …. The span of some vectors is the set of every point you can reach that way.

glossary.def: a sum of scaled vectors.
all linear combinations of a set of vectors.
the scalar multiplying a vector.
the possible shapes of a span in 2D.

math/linear-independence-and-basis.title: Linear Independence and Basis
math/linear-independence-and-basis.summary: Vectors are linearly independent if none of them can be built from the others, and a basis is a smallest set of independent vectors that spans a space.

glossary.def: no vector is a combination of the others.
independent vectors that span the space.
the number of vectors in a basis.
the coefficients of a vector in a basis.

math/norms-and-distance.title: Norms and Distance
math/norms-and-distance.summary: A norm measures the size of a vector, and the distance between two vectors is the norm of their difference.

glossary.def: a measure of a vector's size.
sum of absolute values, Euclidean length, largest component.
a vector of length 1.

math/dot-product.title: Dot Product
math/dot-product.summary: The dot product multiplies two vectors into one number by multiplying matching components and adding: a · b = a₁b₁ + a₂b₂ + ….

glossary.def: the sum of products of matching components.
perpendicular, with dot product zero.
the shadow of one vector on another.
a dot product of weights and inputs.

math/cosine-similarity.title: Cosine Similarity
math/cosine-similarity.summary: Cosine similarity measures how closely two vectors point in the same direction, ignoring how long they are: cos θ = (a · b) / (‖a‖ ‖b‖).

glossary.def: the cosine of the angle between two vectors.
rescaling a vector to length 1.
the turn from one vector to the other.
a vector representing a word, image or item.

math/matrices-as-transformations.title: Matrices as Transformations
math/matrices-as-transformations.summary: A matrix is a grid of numbers, and multiplying a vector by a matrix transforms it: stretching, rotating, flipping or shearing space.

glossary.def: a rectangular grid of numbers.
a warp that keeps lines straight and fixes the origin.
where a basis vector lands.
common transformations.

math/matrix-multiplication.title: Matrix Multiplication
math/matrix-multiplication.summary: Matrix multiplication combines two matrices into one that does both transformations in a row. Each entry of the result is a dot product of a row of the first matrix with a column of the second.

glossary.def: the matrix combining two transformations.
the shared size that must match.
the order changes the result.
many inputs multiplied at once.

math/transpose-identity-and-inverse.title: Transpose, Identity and Inverse
math/transpose-identity-and-inverse.summary: Three special matrix ideas come up constantly: the transpose (flip rows and columns), the identity (the matrix that does nothing) and the inverse (the matrix that undoes another).

glossary.def: swapping rows and columns.
the matrix that leaves vectors unchanged.
the matrix that undoes another.
having no inverse (determinant zero).

math/determinant.title: Determinant
math/determinant.summary: The determinant of a square matrix is a single number telling you how the transformation scales area (or volume): a determinant of 3 makes shapes three times larger, 0.5 halves them, 0 flattens…

glossary.def: the signed factor by which a matrix scales area or volume.
a matrix with determinant zero.
whether a transformation preserves or flips handedness.
the image of the unit square.

math/solving-linear-systems.title: Solving Linear Systems
math/solving-linear-systems.summary: A linear system is several linear equations that must all hold at once, such as x + y = 5 and x − y = 1.

glossary.def: several linear equations solved together.
cancelling unknowns by combining equations.
having / lacking a solution.
the matrix A in A x = b.

math/rank-and-null-space.title: Rank and Null Space
math/rank-and-null-space.summary: The rank of a matrix is the number of independent directions it keeps, and its null space is the set of inputs it sends to zero.

glossary.def: the number of independent columns.
all outputs of a matrix.
the inputs mapped to zero.
as much rank as the matrix's smaller dimension allows.

math/orthogonality-and-projection.title: Orthogonality and Projection
math/orthogonality-and-projection.summary: Two vectors are orthogonal when their dot product is zero (they meet at a right angle), and the projection of one vector onto another is its shadow: the closest point to it along the other's…

glossary.def: perpendicular, dot product zero.
the shadow of one vector on another.
the part left after projecting.
orthogonal and of length 1.

math/least-squares.title: Least Squares
math/least-squares.summary: When a system of equations has more equations than unknowns, it usually has no exact solution. Least squares finds the values that come closest, by minimising the total squared error.

glossary.def: choosing parameters that minimise the sum of squared errors.
the difference between a target and its prediction.
AᵀA x = Aᵀb.
a point far from the pattern.

math/eigenvalues-and-eigenvectors.title: Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors
math/eigenvalues-and-eigenvectors.summary: An eigenvector of a matrix is a direction that the matrix only stretches, without turning: A v = λ v. The stretch factor λ is its eigenvalue.

glossary.def: a direction only scaled by a matrix.
the scaling factor along an eigenvector.
det(A − λI) = 0.
the sum of a matrix's diagonal entries.

math/svd-and-pca.title: SVD and PCA
math/svd-and-pca.summary: The singular value decomposition (SVD) breaks any matrix into a rotation, a stretch along perpendicular axes, and another rotation: A = U Σ Vᵀ.

glossary.def: the factorisation A = U Σ Vᵀ.
a stretch factor in Σ.
a direction of maximal variance.
the share of total variance a component holds.

math/tensors-and-shapes.title: Tensors and Shapes
math/tensors-and-shapes.summary: A tensor is a grid of numbers with any number of dimensions: a scalar is 0-dimensional, a vector 1-dimensional, a matrix 2-dimensional, and a stack of images 4-dimensional.

glossary.def: a grid of numbers with any number of dimensions.
the size of each dimension.
stretching size-1 dimensions to fit.
changing the shape while keeping the entries.

math/calculus.title: Calculus
math/calculus.summary: Calculus is the maths of change. It answers "how fast is this quantity changing right now?" (differentiation) and "how much has it accumulated?" (integration).

math/rate-of-change.title: Rate of Change
math/rate-of-change.summary: A rate of change says how much one quantity changes per unit of another, such as kilometres per hour or dollars per item.

glossary.def: change in output over change in input.
the rate at a single point.
a line through two points of a curve.
the line that touches a curve at a point.

math/limits.title: Limits
math/limits.summary: A limit is the value a function approaches as its input gets closer and closer to some point, even if the function never actually reaches (or is not even defined at) that point.

glossary.def: the value a function approaches.
the value approached from just one side.
an expression like 0/0 that needs simplifying.
a value approached at infinity.

math/continuity.title: Continuity
math/continuity.summary: A function is continuous at a point when you can draw it through that point without lifting your pen: the limit exists and equals the function's value.

glossary.def: no jump or hole at the point.
a point where continuity fails.
having derivatives of all needed orders.
a point of sudden slope change.

math/derivatives.title: Derivatives
math/derivatives.summary: The derivative tells you how fast a function's output is changing at one particular input: the slope of the curve at a point.

glossary.def: the instantaneous rate of change; the slope of the tangent.
the line that just touches a curve at a point.
a line through two points of a curve.
a point where the derivative is zero.

math/derivative-rules.title: Derivative Rules
math/derivative-rules.summary: You do not compute a derivative from the limit every time.

glossary.def: d/dx xⁿ = n xⁿ⁻¹.
the derivative of a product.
the derivative of a ratio.
derivatives pass through sums and constant multiples.

math/chain-rule.title: Chain Rule
math/chain-rule.summary: The chain rule finds the derivative of a function built from other functions: d/dx f(g(x)) = f′(g(x)) · g′(x). Rates multiply along the chain, like gears turning one another.

glossary.def: the derivative of a composition is a product of derivatives.
the function applied first / last.
a function built by chaining others.
the chain rule applied through a network.

math/derivatives-of-exp-log-and-sigmoid.title: Derivatives of Exp, Log and Sigmoid
math/derivatives-of-exp-log-and-sigmoid.path: Math/Calculus/Derivatives of Exp, Log and Sigmoid.md
math/derivatives-of-exp-log-and-sigmoid.summary: Three families of functions carry most of machine learning: the exponential eˣ, the natural logarithm ln x, and the sigmoid σ(x).

glossary.def: eˣ, equal to its own derivative.
ln x, the inverse of eˣ.
1 / (1 + e⁻ˣ), with slope σ(1 − σ).
slopes shrinking toward zero through many layers.

math/higher-derivatives-and-curvature.title: Higher Derivatives and Curvature
math/higher-derivatives-and-curvature.summary: The second derivative is the derivative of the derivative: it says how the slope itself is changing. Positive means the curve bends upward like a bowl, negative means it bends downward like a hill.

glossary.def: the derivative of the derivative.
curving like a bowl / a hill.
how quickly the slope changes.
where the bend changes direction.

math/partial-derivatives.title: Partial Derivatives
math/partial-derivatives.summary: A partial derivative measures how a function of several variables changes when you nudge one variable and hold the others fixed.

glossary.def: the derivative in one variable, others held fixed.
a one-variable cross-section of a surface.
the graph of a two-variable function.
treating other variables as constants.

math/gradients.title: Gradients
math/gradients.summary: The gradient collects all the partial derivatives of a function into one vector, ∇f = (∂f/∂x, ∂f/∂y, …).

glossary.def: the vector of partial derivatives.
the direction of fastest increase.
a path of constant function value.
where the gradient is zero.

math/jacobian.title: Jacobian
math/jacobian.summary: The Jacobian is the matrix of all first partial derivatives of a function that takes several inputs and gives several outputs.

glossary.def: the matrix of first partial derivatives.
replacing a function by its Jacobian near a point.
a function with several outputs.
the local area scaling.

math/hessian.title: Hessian
math/hessian.summary: The Hessian is the matrix of all second partial derivatives of a function.

glossary.def: the matrix of second partial derivatives.
a flat spot that rises in some directions and falls in others.
all eigenvalues positive (a bowl).
the ratio of largest to smallest eigenvalue.

math/integrals.title: Integrals
math/integrals.summary: An integral adds up a quantity that changes continuously: the area under a curve.

glossary.def: the area under a curve.
a function whose derivative is the given one.
a sum of thin bar areas.

math/taylor-approximation.title: Taylor Approximation
math/taylor-approximation.summary: A Taylor approximation replaces a complicated function near a point by a simple polynomial built from its derivatives there.

glossary.def: a polynomial built from a function's derivatives at a point.
the highest power kept.
what the approximation leaves out.
the first-order approximation.

math/automatic-differentiation.title: Automatic Differentiation
math/automatic-differentiation.summary: Automatic differentiation (autodiff) is how software computes exact derivatives: it records each operation in a computational graph, then applies the chain rule backwards through that graph.

glossary.def: operations and values drawn as a graph.
computing values from inputs to output.
propagating derivatives from output to inputs.
the method behind backpropagation.

math/probability.title: Probability
math/probability.summary: Probability is the maths of uncertainty. It gives numbers to "how likely?", and rules for combining those numbers.

math/events-and-sample-spaces.title: Events and Sample Spaces
math/events-and-sample-spaces.summary: A sample space is the set of all outcomes that could happen, and an event is any collection of those outcomes.

glossary.def: the set of all possible outcomes.
a subset of the sample space.
one possible result.
each outcome having the same probability.

math/probability-rules.title: Probability Rules
math/probability-rules.summary: Every probability, however it is produced, obeys a short list of rules: it lies between 0 and 1, the whole sample space has probability 1, the probability of "not A" is 1 − P(A), and for "A or B"…

glossary.def: the event that A does not happen.
P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B).
the events cannot both happen.
the basic rules all probabilities obey.

math/conditional-probability.title: Conditional Probability
math/conditional-probability.summary: Conditional probability is the probability of an event given that another has happened: P(A | B), read "the probability of A given B".

glossary.def: P(A | B), the probability of A given B.
P(A and B) = P(A | B) P(B).
what is assumed to have happened.
the outcomes consistent with B.

math/independence.title: Independence
math/independence.summary: Two events are independent when knowing one happened tells you nothing about the other: P(A | B) = P(A). Equivalently, the probability of both is the product: P(A and B) = P(A) · P(B).

glossary.def: one gives no information about the other.
P(A and B) = P(A) P(B) for independent events.
not independent.
believing past independent trials affect the next.

math/bayes-theorem.title: Bayes Theorem
math/bayes-theorem.summary: Bayes' theorem is the rule for updating how likely you think something is after you see new evidence: P(H | E) = P(E | H) · P(H) / P(E).

glossary.def: P(H | E) = P(E | H) P(H) / P(E).
the probability before seeing evidence.
the probability of the evidence given the hypothesis.
the probability after seeing evidence.
how common the hypothesis is overall.

math/random-variables.title: Random Variables
math/random-variables.summary: A random variable is a number whose value depends on chance: the total of two dice, the number of heads in ten flips, a model's error on the next example.

glossary.def: a number determined by chance.
separate values / any value in a range.
the list of probabilities for a discrete variable.
the pattern of how likely each value is.

math/expectation.title: Expectation
math/expectation.summary: The expectation (or mean) of a random variable is its long-run average: each value weighted by its probability.

glossary.def: the probability-weighted average.
E[aX + bY] = aE[X] + bE[Y].
another name for the expectation.
estimating an expectation by averaging samples.

math/variance-and-standard-deviation.title: Variance and Standard Deviation
math/variance-and-standard-deviation.summary: Variance measures how spread out a random variable is around its mean: the average squared distance from the mean.

glossary.def: the mean squared distance from the mean.
the square root of the variance.
how far values typically lie from the centre.
subtracting the mean and dividing by the standard deviation.

math/discrete-distributions.title: Discrete Distributions
math/discrete-distributions.summary: A few discrete distributions describe most counting situations.

glossary.def: one experiment with two outcomes.
the number of successes in n independent trials.
counts of rare independent events in an interval.
the average number of events per interval.

math/continuous-distributions.title: Continuous Distributions
math/continuous-distributions.summary: A continuous random variable can take any value in a range, so no single value has positive probability.

glossary.def: a curve whose area gives probability.
the bell curve set by mean and standard deviation.
the distance from the mean in standard deviations.
waiting times with a constant rate.

math/joint-and-marginal-distributions.title: Joint and Marginal Distributions
math/joint-and-marginal-distributions.summary: A joint distribution gives the probability of every combination of two or more random variables at once.

glossary.def: probabilities of combinations of variables.
one variable's distribution, summing out the others.
a variable's distribution given another's value.
P(x, y) = P(x) P(y | x).

math/law-of-large-numbers.title: Law of Large Numbers
math/law-of-large-numbers.summary: The law of large numbers says that the average of many independent repetitions settles down to the expectation. Flip a fair coin enough times and the fraction of heads approaches one half.

glossary.def: sample means converge to the expectation.
the average of the observations.
getting arbitrarily close.
the spread of a sample mean, σ / √n.

math/central-limit-theorem.title: Central Limit Theorem
math/central-limit-theorem.summary: The central limit theorem says that the average (or sum) of many independent random values follows a bell curve, whatever shape the individual values have. Its spread shrinks as σ / √n.

glossary.def: sample means become normal as n grows.
σ / √n, the spread of a sample mean.
the distribution of a statistic over repeated samples.
using the bell curve as a stand-in.

math/markov-chains.title: Markov Chains
math/markov-chains.summary: A Markov chain is a sequence of random states where the next state depends only on the current one, not on how you got there.

glossary.def: a random sequence where the next state depends only on the current state.
the table of probabilities of moving between states.
a distribution unchanged by a step.
the future depends on the present, not the past.

math/statistics.title: Statistics
math/statistics.summary: Probability reasons from a known chance process to what data it will produce. Statistics runs the other way: it starts from data and reasons back to what produced it.

math/describing-data.title: Describing Data
math/describing-data.summary: A few numbers can summarise a whole data set: where its centre is (mean, median, mode) and how spread out it is (range, variance, standard deviation, quartiles).

glossary.def: average, middle value, most frequent value.
measures of spread.
a value marking 25%, 50% or 75% of the sorted data.
the range of the middle half of the data.

math/data-distributions-and-outliers.title: Data Distributions and Outliers
math/data-distributions-and-outliers.summary: The shape of a data set, its distribution, tells you which summaries make sense and which models will work.

glossary.def: bars showing how many values fall in each bin.
asymmetry, with a long tail on one side.
a picture of the quartiles and outliers.
a value far from the rest.

math/sampling-and-bias.title: Sampling and Bias
math/sampling-and-bias.summary: A sample is the part of a population you actually observe, and statistics uses it to say something about the whole.

glossary.def: everyone of interest / the part observed.
every member has an equal chance of selection.
systematic exclusion in how the sample is chosen.
the typical random error of a sample mean.

math/covariance-and-correlation.title: Covariance and Correlation
math/covariance-and-correlation.summary: Covariance measures whether two variables tend to be above or below their means together.

glossary.def: the average product of the two variables' deviations.
covariance scaled to −1 to 1.
a table of all pairwise covariances.
a straight-line relationship.

math/correlation-vs-causation.title: Correlation vs Causation
math/correlation-vs-causation.summary: Two quantities are correlated when they tend to move together, but that alone does not mean one causes the other.

glossary.def: a tendency to move together.
one thing bringing about another.
a hidden common cause.
assigning conditions by chance to isolate cause.

math/estimation-and-bias.title: Estimation and Bias
math/estimation-and-bias.summary: An estimator is a recipe for guessing an unknown quantity from data, such as using the sample mean to estimate the population mean.

glossary.def: a rule for estimating an unknown from data.
the average error of an estimator.
how much it varies between samples.
having zero bias.

math/maximum-likelihood.title: Maximum Likelihood
math/maximum-likelihood.summary: Maximum likelihood estimation picks the parameter value that makes the observed data as probable as possible.

glossary.def: the probability of the data as a function of the parameters.
the parameter maximising the likelihood.
the logarithm of the likelihood.
the loss obtained by flipping the sign.

math/confidence-intervals.title: Confidence Intervals
math/confidence-intervals.summary: A confidence interval is a range built from a sample that expresses how uncertain an estimate is: "the average is 52, give or take about 2".

glossary.def: a range from a procedure that captures the truth a stated share of the time.
that share, such as 95%.
the standard deviation of an estimate.
half the width of the interval.

math/hypothesis-testing-and-p-values.title: Hypothesis Testing and P-values
math/hypothesis-testing-and-p-values.summary: A hypothesis test asks whether a result could plausibly be due to chance alone.

glossary.def: the "no effect" assumption.
the probability of data at least this extreme if the null is true.
the threshold below which we reject the null.
the number summarising the data for the test.

math/common-test-mistakes.title: Common Test Mistakes
math/common-test-mistakes.summary: Statistical tests are easy to misuse.

glossary.def: false positives multiplying with the number of tests.
dividing α by the number of tests.
analysing until a result is significant.
the chance of detecting a real effect.

math/bayesian-vs-frequentist.title: Bayesian vs Frequentist
math/bayesian-vs-frequentist.summary: Statisticians have two philosophies. Frequentists treat probability as a long-run frequency and parameters as fixed but unknown numbers, so they ask how data would behave over repeated experiments.

glossary.def: probability as long-run frequency.
probability as a degree of belief.
belief before / after seeing data.
a prior that keeps the posterior in the same family (Beta for coins).

math/overfitting-in-statistics.title: Overfitting in Statistics
math/overfitting-in-statistics.summary: Overfitting happens when a model fits the quirks and noise of its training data instead of the underlying pattern, so it does well on the data it saw and badly on new data.

glossary.def: fitting noise, so performance on new data is worse.
a model too simple to capture the pattern.
data held back to measure generalisation.
rotating the held-out part.

math/information-theory.title: Information Theory
math/information-theory.summary: Information theory measures uncertainty and surprise in numbers.

math/surprise-and-information.title: Surprise and Information
math/surprise-and-information.summary: The information (or surprise) of an event is −log₂ p bits, where p is its probability. A certain event carries no information, a fair coin flip carries one bit, and a very rare event carries a lot.

glossary.def: −log p, how unexpected an event is.
the information in one fair yes/no answer.
information measured with the natural logarithm.
another name for surprise.

math/entropy.title: Entropy
math/entropy.summary: Entropy is the average surprise of a distribution: H = −Σ p log₂ p. It measures how uncertain an outcome is before you see it.

glossary.def: the average surprise of a distribution.
a unit of information (log base 2).
all outcomes equally likely, with maximum entropy.
the reduction in entropy after learning something.

math/joint-and-conditional-entropy.title: Joint and Conditional Entropy
math/joint-and-conditional-entropy.summary: Joint entropy H(X, Y) is the uncertainty of two variables together, and conditional entropy H(Y | X) is the uncertainty left in Y once you know X.

glossary.def: the uncertainty of two variables together.
the uncertainty left in one after knowing another.
H(X, Y) = H(X) + H(Y | X).
fixed exactly by another variable.

math/cross-entropy.title: Cross-Entropy
math/cross-entropy.summary: Cross-entropy is the average surprise you feel when the world follows distribution p but you predicted with distribution q: H(p, q) = −Σ p log q.

glossary.def: the average surprise using prediction q when reality is p.
a target with probability 1 on a single class.

math/kl-divergence.title: KL Divergence

math/mutual-information.title: Mutual Information
math/mutual-information.summary: Mutual information I(X; Y) measures how much knowing one variable reduces your uncertainty about the other.

math/optimization.title: Optimization
math/optimization.summary: Optimization is the art of finding the best values: the parameters that make a model's error as small as possible.

math/loss-functions.title: Loss Functions
math/loss-functions.summary: A loss function turns "how wrong is the model?" into a single number: small when predictions are good, large when they are bad.

glossary.def: a number measuring how wrong predictions are.
mean squared / mean absolute error.
the negative log of the probability given to the truth.

math/minima-maxima-and-saddle-points.title: Minima, Maxima and Saddle Points
math/minima-maxima-and-saddle-points.summary: A minimum is a low point of a function, a maximum a high point, and a saddle point is flat but rises in some directions and falls in others.

glossary.def: where the gradient is zero.
lowest nearby / lowest overall.

math/gradient-descent.title: Gradient Descent
math/gradient-descent.summary: Gradient descent finds a minimum by repeatedly stepping downhill: compute the gradient (the uphill direction), move a little the opposite way, and repeat.

glossary.def: repeatedly stepping against the gradient.
the step-size multiplier.
one update of the parameters.
settling near a minimum.

math/learning-rate.title: Learning Rate
math/learning-rate.summary: The learning rate η sets how big each gradient-descent step is. Too small and training crawls; too large and it overshoots, bounces around, or blows up.

glossary.def: the step-size multiplier η.

bouncing across a minimum.
changing η over training.

math/convex-vs-non-convex.title: Convex vs Non-Convex
math/convex-vs-non-convex.summary: A function is convex if it is bowl-shaped: the straight line between any two points on its graph never dips below the graph.

math/stochastic-gradient-descent.title: Stochastic Gradient Descent
math/stochastic-gradient-descent.summary: Stochastic gradient descent (SGD) takes each step using the gradient from a small random mini-batch of examples instead of the whole data set.

glossary.def: a small random subset of the data.
one full pass through the data.
correct on average.
the number of examples per step.

math/momentum-and-adam.title: Momentum and Adam
math/momentum-and-adam.summary: Momentum lets a walker keep some of its previous velocity, so it speeds up along steady slopes and smooths out zig-zags.

glossary.def: keeping a running velocity of past gradients.
an optimiser with momentum and per-parameter step sizes.
rescaling early running averages.

math/constraints-and-lagrange-multiplier.title: Constraints and Lagrange Multipliers
math/constraints-and-lagrange-multiplier.summary: Often you want the best value subject to a condition: the cheapest plan that still meets a target, or the largest area for a fixed perimeter.

glossary.def: a condition the solution must satisfy.

math/regularization-as-a-constraint.title: Regularization as a Constraint
math/regularization-as-a-constraint.summary: Regularization keeps a model from fitting noise by discouraging large weights: add a penalty such as λ‖w‖² to the loss.

glossary.def: limiting model complexity to reduce overfitting.
penalising squared weights.
penalising absolute weights.
having many exactly-zero entries.

math/numerical-computing.summary: Computers do not do real-number maths exactly.

math/floating-point.title: Floating Point
math/floating-point.summary: Computers store real numbers in floating point: a fixed number of significant binary digits and an exponent.

glossary.def: storing a number as mantissa times a power of two.
the gap between 1 and the next representable number.
the number of significant bits.
the difference between the true value and the stored one.

math/overflow-and-underflow.title: Overflow and Underflow
math/overflow-and-underflow.summary: Overflow happens when a result is too large to store and becomes infinity; underflow happens when it is too small and becomes zero.

glossary.def: a result too large to store, becoming infinity.
a result too small to store, becoming zero.

working with logarithms of values to avoid extremes.

math/numerical-stability.title: Numerical Stability
math/numerical-stability.summary: A formula that is correct on paper can give wrong answers on a computer, because rounding errors get magnified.

math/conditioning.title: Conditioning
math/conditioning.summary: A problem is ill-conditioned when tiny changes in its input cause huge changes in its answer, no matter how carefully you compute. The condition number measures that sensitivity.

glossary.def: the ratio of largest to smallest stretch of a matrix.
very sensitive to small changes.

modifying a problem to improve its conditioning.

math/random-numbers-and-seeds.title: Random Numbers and Seeds
math/random-numbers-and-seeds.summary: Computers cannot produce true randomness by calculation, so they use pseudo-random number generators: deterministic recipes that produce sequences that look random. The seed is the starting value.

math/logistic-regression-and-the-sigmoid.path: Math/Math in AI/Logistic Regression and the Sigmoid.md

math/a-forward-pass-by-hand.title: A Forward Pass by Hand
math/a-forward-pass-by-hand.path: Math/Math in AI/A Forward Pass by Hand.md
math/a-forward-pass-by-hand.summary: A forward pass pushes an input through a network layer by layer to produce a prediction. Each layer is the same recipe: multiply by a weight matrix, add a bias, apply an activation function.

glossary.def: computing the output from the input through the layers.
a layer between input and output.
the value before / after the activation function.
the constant added in each layer.

math/backpropagation-by-hand.title: Backpropagation by Hand
math/backpropagation-by-hand.summary: Backpropagation computes how the loss changes with every weight in a network by applying the chain rule backwards from the output. Its results are exactly the gradients that gradient descent needs.

glossary.def: applying the chain rule backwards through a network.
the derivative of one node's output with respect to its input.

math/softmax-and-cross-entropy-in-practi.title: Softmax and Cross-Entropy in Practice
math/softmax-and-cross-entropy-in-practi.path: Math/Math in AI/Softmax and Cross-Entropy in Practice.md
math/softmax-and-cross-entropy-in-practi.summary: For questions with many possible answers, a network outputs one raw score (a logit) per class.

math/embeddings-and-similarity-search.title: Embeddings and Similarity Search
math/embeddings-and-similarity-search.path: Math/Math in AI/Embeddings and Similarity Search.md
math/embeddings-and-similarity-search.summary: An embedding represents a word, image, song or user as a vector of numbers, learned so that similar things end up close together.

math/attention-as-dot-products.title: Attention as Dot Products

math/bias-variance-and-the-whole-picture.title: Bias, Variance and the Whole Picture
math/bias-variance-and-the-whole-picture.path: Math/Math in AI/Bias, Variance and the Whole Picture.md
math/bias-variance-and-the-whole-picture.summary: A model's error on new data comes from three sources: bias (the model is too simple to capture the pattern), variance (the model is so flexible it changes wildly with the particular training data)…

the trained process of removing noise step by step, used to generate new samples.

the aggregate-then-update pattern a GNN layer performs.
one edge's worth of distance in a graph; a GNN with k layers can reach information up to k hops away.

the simplest way to numerically solve a differential equation, taking fixed-size steps along the rate of change.
letting a solver choose smaller steps where accuracy requires it and larger steps where it doesn't.

the small network that scores and selects which experts handle a given input.
keeping only the k highest-scoring experts and renormalising their weights.

removing the smallest-magnitude weights specifically.
the fraction of a network's weights that have been pruned (set to zero).

the spacing between adjacent quantization levels, determined by the value range and bit-width.
converting a quantized integer code back into its approximate real value.

glossary.def: the large, already-trained model and the smaller model being trained to mimic it.

an empirical power-law relationship between loss and model size, data, or compute.
floating-point operations, the unit used to measure and budget training compute.

deliberately training a smaller model on more tokens than compute-optimal scaling would allocate, to reduce inference cost.
steadily shrinking improvement per additional unit of the variable being increased.

the sharp rise in accuracy across a comparatively narrow band of scale.

the compute level at which a scaled-generic method's performance overtakes a hand-engineered method's.

one training example consisting of a user instruction and an ideal assistant response.
learning to reproduce the pattern of given examples, without an explicit signal about why they were chosen.

generating more instructions by applying varied phrasings or framings to each seed.
using a model to generate new instructions from a seed set, rather than fixed templates.

llms/reward-modeling.title: Reward Modeling

a model of pairwise comparison outcomes as a function of two latent scalar scores.

llms/fine-tuning-for-a-specific-task.summary: An aligned, general-purpose assistant is often not what a product actually needs — a narrower model trained specifically on one job's data can do that one job better, cheaper, and more predictably.

updating every parameter of the base model during fine-tuning.
adding a small number of new parameters (two low-rank matrices) on top of a frozen base model, as in LoRA.

glossary.def: the loss of a model's prior capability caused by further training on a new task.
the single set of parameters that every task's gradient update moves, with no separation between what's "for" one task and what's "for" another.
the relationship between how much a model improves on a new task and how much it degrades on tasks it previously performed well.

the token cost incurred repeatedly on every single request, regardless of how short the user's own message is.

masking decoding so that only schema-valid tokens can ever be produced, removing parse failures by construction.

taking the parameter-by-parameter mean of two models' weights to produce a single combined model.
a model fine-tuned for strong performance on one specific task, typically at the cost of weaker performance elsewhere.

generating a request's output tokens one at a time, each depending on all previous ones, so comparatively slow per token.
charging separately, and usually at different rates, for input and output tokens.

a single number combining a model's scores across several dimensions, according to a chosen set of weights.
choosing which available model to deploy for a task, based on how well it matches that task's specific requirements.

llms/guardrails-and-deployment-time-safe.summary: Alignment training shapes what a model tends to do on its own, but a deployed product rarely relies on that alone.

the fraction of genuinely unsafe content a filter successfully blocks.

the per-request cost and latency incurred once a model is serving live traffic, separate from however it was trained.

rag/why-retrieval-and-grounding.summary: A model's weights are a fixed snapshot of what it learned during training — they can't be updated with this morning's news or a document it's never seen.

information kept in an external, searchable store, updatable immediately without touching the model.
combining a model's parametric knowledge with non-parametric knowledge fetched from a document store at answer-time.

rag/hallucination-and-knowledge-cutoff.title: Hallucination and Knowledge Cutoff

rag/hallucination-and-knowledge-cutoff.summary: Every model has a training cutoff — a date after which nothing happened in its training data. Ask it about something before that date, and it usually answers confidently and correctly.

glossary.def: the date after which no data existed in a model's training set.
a model producing a confident, fluent answer that is factually wrong.
the gradual drop in reliability of a model's unretrieved answers as a question moves further past its training cutoff.

rag/rag-vs-fine-tuning-vs-long-context.path: RAG/Why Retrieval and Grounding/RAG vs. Fine-Tuning vs. Long-Context.md
rag/rag-vs-fine-tuning-vs-long-context.summary: A model that doesn't know something, or doesn't behave the way you want, has more than one fix available.

glossary.def: supplying potentially relevant information directly in the prompt rather than searching for it, limited by the context window and its per-request cost.
the general choice of mechanism (retrieval, fine-tuning, long-context, or some combination) used to close a gap between a model's default behavior and what a task needs.
how quickly a change in the real world can be reflected in a system's answers.

glossary.def: the user's raw question before any processing.
the number of highest-scoring documents kept after retrieval, out of the full collection.
arranging retrieved passages into the prompt the model will actually generate from.

rag/parsing-documents-for-retrieval.path: RAG/Document Processing and Chunking/Parsing Documents for Retrieval.md

converting a document's native format into clean text suitable for chunking.
the share of a raw extraction that turns out to be boilerplate rather than real content.

rag/fixed-size-and-recursive-chunking.title: Fixed-Size and Recursive Chunking

splitting on structural units (paragraphs, sentences) and packing them up to a size limit without ever cutting one in half.
the point where one chunk ends and the next begins.

rag/semantic-and-structure-aware-chunkin.summary: Recursive chunking keeps sentences whole, but a sentence boundary isn't the same thing as a topic boundary — five sentences in a row about the same subject will still get split wherever the size…

glossary.def: placing chunk boundaries where consecutive sentences' embedding similarity drops, rather than at a fixed size.
splitting at a document's own structural markers (headings, paragraphs) instead of computing similarity.
the cutoff below which two consecutive sentences are considered different enough to warrant a chunk boundary.

rag/chunk-overlap-and-size-trade-offs.title: Chunk Overlap and Size Trade-offs
rag/chunk-overlap-and-size-trade-offs.path: RAG/Document Processing and Chunking/Chunk Overlap and Size Trade-offs.md
rag/chunk-overlap-and-size-trade-offs.summary: A fact that happens to straddle a chunk boundary disappears — split in half across two chunks, it may be incomplete in both and never score high enough against a query to be retrieved.

glossary.def: the number of characters (or tokens) repeated between the end of one chunk and the start of the next.
the fraction of total stored characters that are duplicates caused by overlap.
a piece of information that falls across where a chunk boundary happens to land, risking being split and lost.

rag/multi-vector-and-late-interaction-re.summary: Pooling every token of a document into one vector means a single, strong, exact match can get diluted by everything else in the document — the more unrelated text surrounds it, the weaker its…

accepting a small risk of missing the true closest results in exchange for a large reduction in search cost.

rag/vector-databases-and-index-managemen.summary: An ANN algorithm like HNSW or IVF answers one question well: given a query, which vectors are closest?
