rag/context-assembly-and-ordering.title: Context Assembly and Ordering
rag/context-assembly-and-ordering.path: RAG/Generation with Retrieved Context/Context Assembly and Ordering.md
rag/context-assembly-and-ordering.summary: Retrieval can rank the single most relevant passage first — and assembly can still bury it in the middle of the prompt, right where a model is statistically least likely to actually use it.

glossary.def: arranging retrieved passages into the final prompt sent to the generating model.
the tendency for information in the middle of a long context to be used less reliably than information at the start or end.
the specific sequence in which retrieved passages are placed within the assembled context.

rag/citation-and-source-attribution.title: Citation and Source Attribution
rag/citation-and-source-attribution.path: RAG/Generation with Retrieved Context/Citation and Source Attribution.md
rag/citation-and-source-attribution.summary: An answer that cites its sources lets a reader check it; an answer that doesn't asks for blind trust.

glossary.def: linking a specific claim in a generated answer to the retrieved passage that supports it.
the broader practice of tracing generated content back to its retrieved origins.
the minimum similarity a claim's best-matching passage must reach to be cited rather than flagged unsupported.

rag/handling-noisy-or-conflicting-retrie.title: Handling Noisy or Conflicting Retrieved Context
rag/handling-noisy-or-conflicting-retrie.path: RAG/Generation with Retrieved Context/Handling Noisy or Conflicting Retrieved Context.md
rag/handling-noisy-or-conflicting-retrie.summary: Retrieval sometimes returns two passages that answer the same question differently — an old policy document and a new one, say, each stating a different number for the same thing.

glossary.def: two or more retrieved passages that answer the same question with different, incompatible information.
resolving a conflict by keeping the most recently dated passage and discarding the others.
retrieved content that is irrelevant, contradictory, or otherwise unhelpful once it reaches generation.

rag/context-window-budgeting-for-rag.title: Context-Window Budgeting for RAG
rag/context-window-budgeting-for-rag.path: RAG/Generation with Retrieved Context/Context-Window Budgeting for RAG.md
rag/context-window-budgeting-for-rag.summary: Retrieved chunks don't get the entire context window to themselves — a running conversation's own history is sitting in there too, and the two are competing for the exact same limited space.

glossary.def: the fixed total token capacity available for a single request's prompt.
how a fixed budget is divided between competing consumers (conversation history, retrieved chunks).
the point at which growing conversation history leaves too little room for retrieved content to contribute meaningfully.

rag/grounded-generation-and-faithfulness.title: Grounded Generation and Faithfulness
rag/grounded-generation-and-faithfulness.path: RAG/Generation with Retrieved Context/Grounded Generation and Faithfulness.md
rag/grounded-generation-and-faithfulness.summary: Retrieving the right passages doesn't guarantee the generated answer actually uses them.

glossary.def: the fraction of a generated answer's claims that are supported by retrieved context.
generation that draws its claims from retrieved context rather than unretrieved, pretrained knowledge.
a generated claim with no sufficiently similar retrieved passage backing it.

rag/evaluating-rag-systems.title: Evaluating RAG Systems
rag/evaluating-rag-systems.summary: A RAG system can fail in two independent places — retrieval can find the wrong passages, or generation can answer badly even from the right ones — and a single end-to-end score can't tell you which.

rag/retrieval-metrics-precision-recall-m.title: Retrieval Metrics: Precision, Recall, MRR and NDCG
rag/retrieval-metrics-precision-recall-m.path: RAG/Evaluating RAG Systems/Retrieval Metrics: Precision, Recall, MRR and NDCG.md
rag/retrieval-metrics-precision-recall-m.summary: Precision and recall, already covered as classification metrics, adapt naturally to retrieval — but a ranked list has structure a classifier's yes/no decision doesn't: where a relevant result…

glossary.def: the reciprocal of the position of the first relevant result in a ranking.
a ranking metric using graded relevance, discounted by position, normalized against the ideal ordering.
a relevance score with more than two levels (not just relevant/irrelevant), as NDCG uses.

rag/faithfulness-and-answer-relevancy-me.title: Faithfulness and Answer Relevancy Metrics
rag/faithfulness-and-answer-relevancy-me.path: RAG/Evaluating RAG Systems/Faithfulness and Answer Relevancy Metrics.md
rag/faithfulness-and-answer-relevancy-me.summary: An answer can be perfectly grounded in its retrieved context and still completely fail to address what was asked — faithful to the wrong thing.

glossary.def: how closely a generated answer's embedding matches the question's embedding.
the fraction of an answer's claims grounded in retrieved context (covered in depth in Grounded Generation and Faithfulness).
two ways an answer can go wrong that don't imply or predict each other.

rag/end-to-end-rag-evaluation-frameworks.title: End-to-End RAG Evaluation Frameworks
rag/end-to-end-rag-evaluation-frameworks.path: RAG/Evaluating RAG Systems/End-to-End RAG Evaluation Frameworks.md
rag/end-to-end-rag-evaluation-frameworks.summary: Two RAG systems can score identically on an overall end-to-end quality check and still be broken in completely different places — one failing at retrieval, the other at generation.

glossary.def: a combined scorecard covering both retrieval-side and generation-side metrics.
retrieval-side metrics measuring how much of the retrieved context is relevant, and how much of the relevant content was retrieved.
identifying which specific pipeline stage (retrieval vs. generation) a low score points to.

rag/common-rag-failure-modes.title: Common RAG Failure Modes
rag/common-rag-failure-modes.path: RAG/Evaluating RAG Systems/Common RAG Failure Modes.md
rag/common-rag-failure-modes.summary: Across this planet's road, the same handful of failure symptoms keep recurring — a stale fact, a result count that's mysteriously short, an answer that confidently cites the wrong thing.

glossary.def: a recurring, recognizable way a RAG system produces a bad result.
associating an observed problem with the specific pipeline stage and technique that addresses it.
the underlying pipeline stage responsible for a surface-level symptom.

rag/synthetic-test-set-generation-for-ra.title: Synthetic Test-Set Generation for RAG
rag/synthetic-test-set-generation-for-ra.path: RAG/Evaluating RAG Systems/Synthetic Test-Set Generation for RAG.md
rag/synthetic-test-set-generation-for-ra.summary: Hand-writing one evaluation question per chunk doesn't scale — a person can write maybe a few dozen good questions in a day, but a real document collection can hold thousands or millions of chunks.

glossary.def: automatically producing (question, answer, source) evaluation triples from a document collection.
the fraction of a corpus that has at least one associated evaluation question.
a generated question paired with its expected answer and the source chunk it was derived from.

rag/a-b-and-online-evaluation-of-rag.title: A-B and Online Evaluation of RAG
rag/a-b-and-online-evaluation-of-rag.path: RAG/Evaluating RAG Systems/A-B and Online Evaluation of RAG.md
rag/a-b-and-online-evaluation-of-rag.summary: A test set, synthetic or hand-written, measures a RAG system against questions someone anticipated.

glossary.def: comparing two system variants by routing real traffic to each and measuring an outcome metric.
measuring a system against real user behavior, as opposed to a fixed offline test set.
whether an observed difference is large enough, relative to sample size, to be distinguishable from random noise.

rag/rag-in-practice.title: RAG in Practice
rag/rag-in-practice.summary: Everything on this road so far has covered one piece of a RAG system at a time.

rag/production-rag-pipeline-architecture.title: Production RAG Pipeline Architecture
rag/production-rag-pipeline-architecture.path: RAG/RAG in Practice/Production RAG Pipeline Architecture.md
rag/production-rag-pipeline-architecture.summary: Every topic on this road so far has zoomed into one stage of a RAG system.

glossary.def: the full chain of stages (embed, search, re-rank, assemble, generate) a real RAG system runs per request.
how a request's total time is divided among its constituent stages.
the overall design of how a RAG system's stages connect and hand off to each other.

rag/caching-and-incremental-indexing.title: Caching and Incremental Indexing
rag/caching-and-incremental-indexing.path: RAG/RAG in Practice/Caching and Incremental Indexing.md
rag/caching-and-incremental-indexing.summary: Asking the same question twice shouldn't cost the full pipeline twice — caching the first answer makes the second one nearly free.

glossary.def: storing and reusing the result of a previous computation (a query's answer, an embedding) instead of recomputing it.
adding new documents to an existing index at a cost proportional to what's added, not the whole collection.
the fraction of requests that can be served from the cache rather than requiring full computation.

rag/cost-and-latency-of-rag-systems.title: Cost and Latency of RAG Systems
rag/cost-and-latency-of-rag-systems.path: RAG/RAG in Practice/Cost and Latency of RAG Systems.md
rag/cost-and-latency-of-rag-systems.summary: A plain LLM call already has its own cost and latency math, already covered on the LLMs planet.

glossary.def: the added latency a RAG pipeline introduces on top of a plain generation call.
the time spent on embedding, searching, and re-ranking, as opposed to generation itself.
added latency expressed as a percentage of the baseline (plain call) latency, which shifts as the baseline itself changes.

rag/security-and-data-leakage-in-rag.title: Security and Data Leakage in RAG
rag/security-and-data-leakage-in-rag.path: RAG/RAG in Practice/Security and Data Leakage in RAG.md
rag/security-and-data-leakage-in-rag.summary: Retrieval is a search over documents, and search has always needed access control — a public user's question shouldn't be able to pull an internal finance document into its retrieved context,…

glossary.def: unauthorized content reaching a user through a system that wasn't supposed to grant them access to it.
restricting retrieval to only chunks a given user is authorized to see.
a retrieved document containing text designed to redirect the generating model's behavior.

rag/capstone-a-question-answered-traced-.title: Capstone: A Question Answered, Traced from Query to Grounded Answer
rag/capstone-a-question-answered-traced-.path: RAG/RAG in Practice/Capstone: A Question Answered, Traced from Query to Grounded Answer.md
rag/capstone-a-question-answered-traced-.summary: Every stage this planet covered separately — retrieving by similarity, re-ranking for accuracy, assembling context sensibly, generating with citations — is usually described one at a time, with…

glossary.def: following one request through every stage of a pipeline in order, rather than examining each stage in isolation.
the reduced set of candidates retrieval passes on to re-ranking.
a generated answer whose claims are verifiably supported by retrieved context.

agents/agents.title: Agents
agents/agents.summary: Every planet before this one covered a model answering one request at a time: a prompt goes in, an answer comes out.

agents/foundations-of-agentic-systems.title: Foundations of Agentic Systems
agents/foundations-of-agentic-systems.path: Agents/Foundations of Agentic Systems/Foundations of Agentic Systems.md
agents/foundations-of-agentic-systems.summary: A single call to a language model, however good, still just returns one response to one prompt.

agents/from-a-single-call-to-a-loop.title: From a Single Call to a Loop
agents/from-a-single-call-to-a-loop.path: Agents/Foundations of Agentic Systems/From a Single Call to a Loop.md
agents/from-a-single-call-to-a-loop.summary: A single call to a model follows exactly one link in a chain of facts, no matter how the chain continues from there.

glossary.def: one request to a model, producing one result, with no further iteration.
repeatedly feeding a result back in and calling again until a goal is met or a budget runs out.
a goal that can't be reached in one step because each step's result is needed to determine the next step.

agents/agents-vs-assistants-vs-workflows.title: Agents vs. Assistants vs. Workflows
agents/agents-vs-assistants-vs-workflows.path: Agents/Foundations of Agentic Systems/Agents vs. Assistants vs. Workflows.md
agents/agents-vs-assistants-vs-workflows.summary: "Agent" gets used loosely enough that a chatbot, a fixed multi-step pipeline, and a genuinely autonomous loop all sometimes get called one.

glossary.def: a single-turn or simply-turn-taking conversational system with no autonomous multi-step drive.
a fixed, developer-coded sequence of calls, predictable but inflexible.
a system that decides its own next step at run-time, flexible but less predictable.

agents/the-augmented-llm.title: The Augmented LLM
agents/the-augmented-llm.path: Agents/Foundations of Agentic Systems/The Augmented LLM.md
agents/the-augmented-llm.summary: A bare model call can only ever draw on what was baked into its weights during training.

glossary.def: a model call combined with tools, memory and retrieval as its three standard additions.
a function an agent can call to take an action or fetch information beyond its own training.
state that persists across turns or runs, as opposed to what's baked into the model's weights.

agents/open-loop-vs-closed-loop-behavior.title: Open-Loop vs. Closed-Loop Behavior
agents/open-loop-vs-closed-loop-behavior.path: Agents/Foundations of Agentic Systems/Open-Loop vs. Closed-Loop Behavior.md
agents/open-loop-vs-closed-loop-behavior.summary: An agent that fires off four actions in a row and reports "done" might be lying — not out of any intent to deceive, but because it never actually checked whether any of those four actions worked.

glossary.def: running a sequence of actions without checking their actual results.
checking each action's real outcome before deciding the next step.
an action that fails without raising any error, detectable only by checking its actual effect.

agents/anatomy-of-an-agent-architecture.title: Anatomy of an Agent Architecture
agents/anatomy-of-an-agent-architecture.path: Agents/Foundations of Agentic Systems/Anatomy of an Agent Architecture.md
agents/anatomy-of-an-agent-architecture.summary: Every agent architecture this road covers, however different the application, is built from the same five named pieces: something that perceives the current request, something that remembers…

glossary.def: the component that reads the current request and any new observations.
the component that decomposes a goal into an ordered sequence of steps.
the component that checks a step's result against the goal and decides whether to loop again.

agents/workflow-patterns-before-autonomy.title: Workflow Patterns Before Autonomy
agents/workflow-patterns-before-autonomy.path: Agents/Workflow Patterns Before Autonomy/Workflow Patterns Before Autonomy.md
agents/workflow-patterns-before-autonomy.summary: Not every multi-step task needs a fully autonomous agent deciding what to do next.

agents/prompt-chaining.title: Prompt Chaining
agents/prompt-chaining.summary: Splitting a task into a fixed sequence of calls — outline, then draft, then polish — lets each step check the previous one's work before building on it.

glossary.def: a fixed sequence of LLM calls, each one's output feeding into the next.
a check between chained steps that verifies an intermediate result before letting it proceed.
a structured, developer-controlled arrangement of calls, as opposed to an autonomous agent's self-directed loop.

agents/routing-between-specialized-promp.title: Routing Between Specialized Prompts
agents/routing-between-specialized-promp.path: Agents/Workflow Patterns Before Autonomy/Routing Between Specialized Prompts.md
agents/routing-between-specialized-promp.summary: One generic handler answering every kind of request is simpler to build than several specialists — and noticeably worse at any one of them.

glossary.def: classifying an incoming request and dispatching it to a specialized prompt built for that category.
a prompt built and tuned for one specific category of request.
the part of routing that determines which category a request belongs to.

agents/parallelization-sectioning-and-vo.title: Parallelization: Sectioning and Voting
agents/parallelization-sectioning-and-vo.path: Agents/Workflow Patterns Before Autonomy/Parallelization: Sectioning and Voting.md
agents/parallelization-sectioning-and-vo.summary: Running three independent pieces of a task one after another wastes time that didn't need to be spent sequentially at all — none of the three pieces needed the others to finish first.

glossary.def: splitting a task into independent subtasks run in parallel, finishing in the time of the slowest piece.
running the same prompt multiple times and taking the most common answer.
each additional sample improving accuracy by a progressively smaller amount.

agents/orchestrator-workers.title: Orchestrator-Workers
agents/orchestrator-workers.summary: A single call asked to analyze a market, project financials, and assess risk, all in one response, often trails off after the first section or two — there was only so much the model would produce…

glossary.def: a pattern where an orchestrator call dynamically decides a task's subtasks, then dispatches one worker call per subtask and assembles the results.
figuring out what a task's pieces are at run time, rather than fixing them in advance.
combining the separate worker calls' outputs into one coherent final result.

agents/evaluator-optimizer-loops.title: Evaluator-Optimizer Loops
agents/evaluator-optimizer-loops.summary: A first draft critiqued once gets noticeably better; critiqued a second time, it gets better still, but by less than the first round did.

glossary.def: a workflow pairing a generating/revising call with an evaluating call that gives feedback, repeated until a stopping condition.
the role that generates or revises a candidate based on feedback.
the role that judges a candidate and returns specific, actionable feedback.

agents/planning-and-task-decomposition.title: Planning and Task Decomposition
agents/planning-and-task-decomposition.path: Agents/Planning and Task Decomposition/Planning and Task Decomposition.md
agents/planning-and-task-decomposition.summary: A genuinely open-ended goal can't be handled by a fixed workflow written in advance — nobody knows the steps until the agent starts looking at the specific situation.

agents/goal-decomposition-into-subtasks.title: Goal Decomposition into Subtasks
agents/goal-decomposition-into-subtasks.path: Agents/Planning and Task Decomposition/Goal Decomposition into Subtasks.md
agents/goal-decomposition-into-subtasks.summary: Told to "launch the product," an agent that lists tasks in whatever order they occur to it can end up trying to launch before the thing it's launching has been tested — the launch step depends on…

glossary.def: breaking a goal into subtasks and the dependencies between them.
a subtask appearing in an order before one of its own prerequisites has completed.
an ordering of a dependency graph's tasks that places every task after all of its prerequisites.

agents/plan-and-execute-agents.title: Plan-and-Execute Agents
agents/plan-and-execute-agents.summary: Deciding every step of a trip itinerary up front, then just following it, takes one planning conversation and one action per stop.

glossary.def: an agent pattern that decomposes a goal into a full ordered plan once, then executes each step without further planning calls.
an agent pattern that reasons about what to do at every step, rather than committing to a plan in advance.
the number of LLM calls an approach needs for a given number of steps.

agents/re-planning-on-failure.title: Re-Planning on Failure
agents/re-planning-on-failure.path: Agents/Planning and Task Decomposition/Re-Planning on Failure.md
agents/re-planning-on-failure.summary: A plan to book a trip hits a hotel that's sold out on step 3 of 5.

glossary.def: detecting that a plan's step failed and generating a new plan for the remaining steps instead of continuing the original one.
later steps failing because they depended on an earlier step's result that never actually materialized.
the moment a failure is actually noticed, which determines how much wasted effort happens before recovery begins.

agents/hierarchical-task-planning.title: Hierarchical Task Planning
agents/hierarchical-task-planning.path: Agents/Planning and Task Decomposition/Hierarchical Task Planning.md
agents/hierarchical-task-planning.summary: "Organize a conference" eventually breaks down into 36 individual primitive actions — booking a specific venue, sending a specific email, printing a specific badge.

glossary.def: a planning approach that decomposes a goal into tasks, then those tasks into sub-tasks, continuing down to primitive actions.
the number of choices a planner has to weigh at a single decision point.
a task simple enough to just be executed, with no further decomposition.

agents/when-planning-hurts-more-than-it-.title: When Planning Hurts More Than It Helps
agents/when-planning-hurts-more-than-it-.path: Agents/Planning and Task Decomposition/When Planning Hurts More Than It Helps.md
agents/when-planning-hurts-more-than-it-.summary: Planning ahead only pays off if the plan is still good by the time it's executed. In a stable environment that barely changes, one upfront plan beats reacting fresh at every single step.

glossary.def: how often the environment changes, measured here as steps between changes (lower volatility means more frequent change).
a plan's one-time cost spread across however many cheap execution steps it stays valid for.
the volatility at which planning and reactive execution cost the same total time.

agents/tool-use-and-function-calling.title: Tool Use and Function Calling
agents/tool-use-and-function-calling.path: Agents/Tool Use and Function Calling/Tool Use and Function Calling.md
agents/tool-use-and-function-calling.summary: Calling one tool correctly is a solved problem, already covered on the LLMs planet.

agents/tool-selection-among-many-candida.title: Tool Selection Among Many Candidates
agents/tool-selection-among-many-candida.path: Agents/Tool Use and Function Calling/Tool Selection Among Many Candidates.md
agents/tool-selection-among-many-candida.summary: An agent with 40 tools available for one task has exactly one that's actually correct. Shown all 40 at once with no other signal to go on, picking it by chance alone succeeds 2.5% of the time.

glossary.def: ranking available tools by relevance to a task and keeping only the top K as candidates for selection.
whether the correct item survives being limited to the top K candidates.
the success rate of a selection that has no signal beyond the candidate set itself.

agents/parallel-vs-sequential-tool-calls.title: Parallel vs. Sequential Tool Calls
agents/parallel-vs-sequential-tool-calls.path: Agents/Tool Use and Function Calling/Parallel vs. Sequential Tool Calls.md
agents/parallel-vs-sequential-tool-calls.summary: Checking flight prices, the weather at the destination, and today's exchange rate are three tool calls that have nothing to do with each other — running them one after another wastes however long…

glossary.def: one tool call needing another call's result as an input.
tool calls with no data dependency between them, which can run in parallel.
a sequence of tool calls where each one needs the previous one's result, forcing sequential execution.

agents/handling-tool-errors-and-retries.title: Handling Tool Errors and Retries
agents/handling-tool-errors-and-retries.path: Agents/Tool Use and Function Calling/Handling Tool Errors and Retries.md
agents/handling-tool-errors-and-retries.summary: A flaky network call that succeeds 70% of the time individually succeeds 99.19% of the time within four tries — failures that are transient are exactly the kind retrying is good for.

glossary.def: a failure with some real chance of not recurring if the same call is tried again.
a failure that will recur identically on every retry, because its cause doesn't change between tries.
the chance that at least one of n independent tries succeeds.

agents/tool-result-verification.title: Tool Result Verification
agents/tool-result-verification.path: Agents/Tool Use and Function Calling/Tool Result Verification.md
agents/tool-result-verification.summary: A weather tool call that returns no exception isn't the same as a weather tool call that actually returned a usable result.

glossary.def: checking that a tool call's returned result actually has the content the next step needs, beyond just confirming the call didn't raise an error.
a tool call that reports success while returning an incomplete or empty result.
a check applied to an intermediate result before letting it proceed to the next step.

agents/designing-tools-for-agent-reliabi.title: Designing Tools for Agent Reliability
agents/designing-tools-for-agent-reliabi.path: Agents/Tool Use and Function Calling/Designing Tools for Agent Reliability.md
agents/designing-tools-for-agent-reliabi.summary: A tool with a free-text date field lets an agent write "03/14/2025," "March 14, 2025," or "14/03/2025" — three formats, at least two of them genuinely ambiguous about which number is the month.

glossary.def: the choices (parameter types, validation strictness, error behavior) that shape how a tool can be called.
a parameter that accepts any string, leaving format ambiguity undetected until the tool tries to use the value.
a parameter definition that only accepts a defined format, rejecting anything else before the tool's own logic runs.

agents/code-as-a-tool-calling-interface.title: Code as a Tool-Calling Interface
agents/code-as-a-tool-calling-interface.path: Agents/Tool Use and Function Calling/Code as a Tool-Calling Interface.md
agents/code-as-a-tool-calling-interface.summary: Applying a discount to 200 items one tool call at a time costs 200 separate round trips, each one a full request and response.

glossary.def: letting a model express an action (including loops and conditionals) as generated code executed in a sandbox, rather than as one discrete structured call per action.
a schema-checked tool call representing exactly one discrete action.
the number of model-to-tool round trips a given approach requires for a task.

agents/memory-and-state-management.title: Memory and State Management
agents/memory-and-state-management.path: Agents/Memory and State Management/Memory and State Management.md
agents/memory-and-state-management.summary: An agent running for hundreds of steps can't keep everything it's ever seen in its context window — and some of what it learns along the way needs to survive past the current run entirely.

agents/short-term-vs-long-term-agent-mem.title: Short-Term vs. Long-Term Agent Memory
agents/short-term-vs-long-term-agent-mem.path: Agents/Memory and State Management/Short-Term vs. Long-Term Agent Memory.md
agents/short-term-vs-long-term-agent-mem.summary: Everything an agent reads during one run — the request, the tool results so far, its own earlier reasoning — disappears the moment that run ends, unless something deliberately writes it somewhere…

glossary.def: the current run's working context, gone once the run ends.
anything deliberately written to external storage that a later, separate run can read back.
to write a fact somewhere that outlives the current run.

agents/episodic-memory-and-experience-lo.title: Episodic Memory and Experience Logs
agents/episodic-memory-and-experience-lo.path: Agents/Memory and State Management/Episodic Memory and Experience Logs.md
agents/episodic-memory-and-experience-lo.summary: The first time an agent faces a task, it has to actually discover which approach works — try something, see it fail, try something else.

glossary.def: a record of a specific task attempt, the approach tried, and its outcome.
a long-term memory store specifically of an agent's own past episodes.
the attempts spent finding a working approach from scratch, paid again by every instance that lacks access to a log of what already worked.

agents/memory-retrieval-as-agent-time-ra.title: Memory Retrieval as Agent-Time RAG
agents/memory-retrieval-as-agent-time-ra.path: Agents/Memory and State Management/Memory Retrieval as Agent-Time RAG.md
agents/memory-retrieval-as-agent-time-ra.summary: An agent with thousands of stored memories can't dump all of them into context on every step — it needs to pull back only the handful actually relevant to what it's doing right now.

glossary.def: running a retrieval step continuously during an agent's task, rather than once per external question.
the collection of an agent's embedded past facts and experiences that retrieval ranks against.
the number of highest-similarity memories actually pulled back for use.

agents/memory-compression-and-forgetting.title: Memory Compression and Forgetting
agents/memory-compression-and-forgetting.path: Agents/Memory and State Management/Memory Compression and Forgetting.md
agents/memory-compression-and-forgetting.summary: A memory store that keeps every fact and every logged episode forever grows without bound — eventually too large to search efficiently, let alone fit anywhere near a context window.

glossary.def: periodically folding older memory entries into a bounded summary.
the raw store size divided by the fixed summarized size.
discarding detail on purpose, as the cost of keeping the overall store at a usable, bounded size.

agents/shared-state-across-a-multi-step-.title: Shared State Across a Multi-Step Task
agents/shared-state-across-a-multi-step-.path: Agents/Memory and State Management/Shared State Across a Multi-Step Task.md
agents/shared-state-across-a-multi-step-.summary: A five-step task that needs today's date can fetch it five separate times, once per step — or fetch it once and write it somewhere every later step can just read.

glossary.def: a store any step of a task can write to and any other step can read from, scoped to that one task's run.
re-retrieving a value another step already obtained, when nothing about that value has changed.
a cached shared value no longer matching the current true value, because something changed after it was written.

agents/multi-agent-systems.title: Multi-Agent Systems
agents/multi-agent-systems.summary: One agent can only hold one line of thought at a time.

agents/supervisor-orchestrator-patterns.title: Supervisor-Orchestrator Patterns
agents/supervisor-orchestrator-patterns.summary: A supervisor agent never does the specialized work itself — it decides which specialist should handle a piece of a task, hands it off, and collects the result.

glossary.def: the single agent that routes subtasks to specialists and collects their results, with no direct specialist-to-specialist communication.
a communication structure where every participant links only to a central hub, never to each other.
a component whose failure disconnects every participant that depended solely on it.

agents/pipeline-and-sequential-handoff.title: Pipeline and Sequential Handoff
agents/pipeline-and-sequential-handoff.summary: A research agent hands its findings to a drafting agent, which hands its draft to a review agent, which hands its approval to a finalizing agent.

glossary.def: a fixed sequence of specialist agents, each handing its output directly to the next.
the point where one stage's output becomes the next stage's input.
a check at a handoff that verifies a stage's output before the next stage runs on it.

agents/swarm-and-peer-to-peer-coordinati.title: Swarm and Peer-to-Peer Coordination
agents/swarm-and-peer-to-peer-coordinati.summary: Remove the supervisor from a star topology and every specialist loses its only connection to the rest of the system at once.

glossary.def: a multi-agent system where agents coordinate directly through shared state, with no central router.
a topology where every pair of agents has a direct link.
a component whose failure disconnects every participant that depended solely on it — present in a star, absent in a mesh.

agents/debate-and-adversarial-multi-agen.title: Debate and Adversarial Multi-Agent Setups
agents/debate-and-adversarial-multi-agen.path: Agents/Multi-Agent Systems/Debate and Adversarial Multi-Agent Setups.md
agents/debate-and-adversarial-multi-agen.summary: A single agent that states a claim has no one checking its arithmetic.

glossary.def: the agent that generates an initial claim or answer.
the agent whose role is to independently check or dispute the proposer's claim.
a multi-agent setup where opposing roles argue a question before a judgment is reached.

agents/role-specialization-in-agent-team.title: Role Specialization in Agent Teams
agents/role-specialization-in-agent-team.path: Agents/Multi-Agent Systems/Role Specialization in Agent Teams.md
agents/role-specialization-in-agent-team.summary: Three identical copies of the same generalist agent are each mediocre at every required skill.

glossary.def: assigning each required skill in a team to an agent built and tuned specifically for it.
an agent built to be adequate across many skills rather than excellent at one.
the overall accuracy across required skills, each scored at whichever agent actually handles it.

agents/coordination-failures-and-deadloc.title: Coordination Failures and Deadlock
agents/coordination-failures-and-deadloc.summary: Two agents, each waiting on a result only the other can produce, aren't making progress — they're stuck in a circular wait.

glossary.def: a cycle of agents each blocked on a result only another in the cycle can produce, so none can proceed.
independent agents each redoing a subtask that only needed to be completed once.
knowledge, available to every relevant agent, of what's already been claimed, completed, or is being waited on.

agents/reflection-and-self-improvement.title: Reflection and Self-Improvement
agents/reflection-and-self-improvement.summary: An agent that never looks back at its own work repeats the same mistake at every step that triggers it.

agents/self-critique-loops-in-agents.title: Self-Critique Loops in Agents
agents/self-critique-loops-in-agents.path: Agents/Reflection and Self-Improvement/Self-Critique Loops in Agents.md
agents/self-critique-loops-in-agents.summary: An arithmetic mistake made at step two of a four-step calculation doesn't stay contained to step two — every later step builds on the wrong number, and the final answer comes out wrong even though…

glossary.def: an agent checking its own last output against what it should have produced, before proceeding.
a mistake at one step silently feeding into and corrupting every step that depends on it.
fixing a detected mistake immediately, before it can affect later steps.

agents/error-attribution-across-a-trajec.title: Error Attribution Across a Trajectory
agents/error-attribution-across-a-trajec.path: Agents/Reflection and Self-Improvement/Error Attribution Across a Trajectory.md
agents/error-attribution-across-a-trajec.summary: A 16-step agent trajectory fails, and the final output is visibly wrong — but the step that actually caused it happened eleven steps earlier, with five more steps run on top of it before anything…

glossary.def: identifying which specific step in a trajectory actually caused an observed failure.
checking a trajectory's steps in order until the broken one is found.
a condition that, once false, stays false for every later step.

agents/learning-from-feedback-without-we.title: Learning from Feedback Without Weight Updates
agents/learning-from-feedback-without-we.path: Agents/Reflection and Self-Improvement/Learning from Feedback Without Weight Updates.md
agents/learning-from-feedback-without-we.summary: An agent that gets told "that approach was wrong, try this instead" and then keeps making the identical mistake on the next attempt hasn't actually used the feedback it was given.

glossary.def: a model's behavior changing based on what's included in its current context, with no weight updates involved.
appending the result or correction from one attempt into the prompt for the next.
a change to a model's trained parameters — explicitly absent from everything in this topic.

agents/verifier-guided-agent-loops.title: Verifier-Guided Agent Loops
agents/verifier-guided-agent-loops.summary: An agent that runs six actions in sequence, one of which is subtly wrong, finds out it failed only once all six are done — by which point the bad action has already fed into whatever came after it.

glossary.def: an agent loop where a separate verifier checks and retries each action immediately, rather than only checking the final result.
the maximum number of retries allowed per action before the loop gives up or escalates.
a problem caught and fixed at the specific action that caused it, rather than requiring the whole trajectory to be redone.

agents/agent-environments-and-action-spa.title: Agent Environments and Action Spaces
agents/agent-environments-and-action-spa.path: Agents/Agent Environments and Action Spaces/Agent Environments and Action Spaces.md
agents/agent-environments-and-action-spa.summary: What an agent can actually do depends entirely on what it's acting inside — clicking around a web page needs a different action space than running shell commands in a terminal.

agents/web-browsing-agents.title: Web-Browsing Agents
agents/web-browsing-agents.path: Agents/Agent Environments and Action Spaces/Web-Browsing Agents.md
agents/web-browsing-agents.summary: A web page an agent is clicking through doesn't hold still: an ad can load, a banner can appear, a list can re-sort, all between the moment the agent decides what to click and the moment the click…

glossary.def: referring to an element by its position in an observed list or DOM order.
referring to an element by a stable identity — a role, id, or visible text — that survives changes elsewhere on the page.
a plan or observation no longer matching the actual state of the world by the time an action executes.

agents/computer-use-agents-and-gui-groun.title: Computer-Use Agents and GUI Grounding
agents/computer-use-agents-and-gui-groun.path: Agents/Agent Environments and Action Spaces/Computer-Use Agents and GUI Grounding.md
agents/computer-use-agents-and-gui-groun.summary: A web agent that can read a page's DOM knows exactly where the Submit button is, by name.

glossary.def: mapping a described or inferred target onto an actual pixel coordinate to act on.
checking whether a predicted click falls within a target's bounding box.
the distance between a predicted click location and the target's true center.

agents/code-execution-agents.title: Code-Execution Agents
agents/code-execution-agents.path: Agents/Agent Environments and Action Spaces/Code-Execution Agents.md
agents/code-execution-agents.summary: Running code one snippet at a time from a clean slate means every new snippet has to re-establish everything the previous ones already set up — reload the data, redefine the variables — before it…

glossary.def: a code environment whose variables and setup persist across separate calls.
a code environment that starts fresh each call, with nothing carried over from before.
a quantity that grows as 1+2+3+...+n, compounding faster than a fixed multiple of n.

agents/hybrid-code-and-gui-action-spaces.title: Hybrid Code-and-GUI Action Spaces
agents/hybrid-code-and-gui-action-spaces.path: Agents/Agent Environments and Action Spaces/Hybrid Code-and-GUI Action Spaces.md
agents/hybrid-code-and-gui-action-spaces.summary: A script can rename fifty files in one call; clicking through a file manager to do the same thing takes fifty clicks.

glossary.def: an action space combining code execution and direct GUI interaction, chosen per step.
a code-based action that completes without error but skips interface logic (like form validation) tied to real user-input events.
choosing the action type for each individual step of a task, rather than committing to one action type for an entire task.

agents/simulated-and-game-environments.title: Simulated and Game Environments
agents/simulated-and-game-environments.path: Agents/Agent Environments and Action Spaces/Simulated and Game Environments.md
agents/simulated-and-game-environments.summary: Training a policy by trial and error means the early trials are, by construction, going to be bad — and letting an agent fail its way to a good policy on a real warehouse robot or a real…

glossary.def: a model of an environment an agent can act in and reset cheaply, standing in for a real one during training or testing.
improving a policy by acting, observing the outcome, and adjusting — which necessarily includes early, bad attempts.
the mismatch between a simulation's dynamics and the real environment's, which can make simulated training results not transfer.

agents/action-space-design-and-its-failu.title: Action-Space Design and Its Failure Modes
agents/action-space-design-and-its-failu.path: Agents/Agent Environments and Action Spaces/Action-Space Design and Its Failure Modes.md
agents/action-space-design-and-its-failu.summary: Giving an agent one distinct action per object it might ever need to pick seems safe — until the number of objects grows and a correct first guess becomes a lottery ticket.

glossary.def: one distinct action per candidate target, whose size grows with the number of candidates.
a generic action with no parameter to specify a target, unable to express which one is meant.
one action type that takes a target as an argument, keeping the space's size constant regardless of candidate count.

agents/evaluating-agents.title: Evaluating Agents
agents/evaluating-agents.summary: Scoring a single generated answer is one problem; scoring a hundred-step trajectory of actions, any one of which could be the reason the whole task failed, is a different and harder one.

agents/agent-benchmarks-and-task-suites.title: Agent Benchmarks and Task Suites
agents/agent-benchmarks-and-task-suites.path: Agents/Evaluating Agents/Agent Benchmarks and Task Suites.md
agents/agent-benchmarks-and-task-suites.summary: A question-answering benchmark checks one generated string against one reference string, and either matches or doesn't.

glossary.def: a task suite that drops an agent into a live environment with a goal, rather than checking one generated output against one reference.
verifying success by inspecting the environment's resulting state rather than matching generated text.
a curated collection of benchmark tasks, often spanning several environments (browsing, coding, tool use).

agents/success-rate-metrics-and-their-bl.title: Success-Rate Metrics and Their Blind Spots
agents/success-rate-metrics-and-their-bl.path: Agents/Evaluating Agents/Success-Rate Metrics and Their Blind Spots.md
agents/success-rate-metrics-and-their-bl.summary: Two agents can share the exact same success rate and still be nowhere near equally good.

glossary.def: the fraction of runs that cross the pass/fail threshold, with no information about how close the rest came.
a continuous measure, between 0 and 1, of how much progress a run made toward the goal.
information a single summary metric discards, here the distance between a failing run and success.

agents/trajectory-level-evaluation.title: Trajectory-Level Evaluation
agents/trajectory-level-evaluation.summary: An agent that takes a forbidden or dangerous action partway through its run, then happens to land on the correct final answer anyway, passes any grader that only checks the final answer.

glossary.def: checking every step of an agent's run, not just its final answer or state.
a pass/fail judgment based solely on the final result, blind to how it was reached.
the fraction of a run's steps judged valid, independent of whether the final outcome was correct.

agents/llm-as-judge-for-agent-trajectori.title: LLM-as-Judge for Agent Trajectories
agents/llm-as-judge-for-agent-trajectori.summary: Checking an agent's full trajectory for soundness, not just its final answer, often has no fixed rule to check against — there's no reference string for "was this a reasonable approach." Using an…

glossary.def: using a model to read and score an agent's full run, applying the same judging mechanism used for single outputs.
a judge's tendency to favor whichever item is shown first, independent of actual quality — unchanged when judging trajectories instead of single outputs.
the full record of an agent's steps, typically far longer than a single generated response.

agents/cost-and-reliability-as-joint-met.title: Cost and Reliability as Joint Metrics
agents/cost-and-reliability-as-joint-met.path: Agents/Evaluating Agents/Cost and Reliability as Joint Metrics.md
agents/cost-and-reliability-as-joint-met.summary: A 95%-success-rate agent sounds better than an 85%-success-rate one, full stop — until the first one costs ten times as much per attempt.

glossary.def: total cost per attempt divided by success rate — the cost of achieving one successful run, accounting for failed attempts.
a configuration that re-attempts a task multiple times to raise its success rate, at a proportional cost.
a single number (like cost per success) that combines two individually incomplete metrics into one that reflects the actual trade-off.

agents/agent-safety-and-governance.title: Agent Safety and Governance
agents/agent-safety-and-governance.path: Agents/Agent Safety and Governance/Agent Safety and Governance.md
agents/agent-safety-and-governance.summary: An agent that can act on the real world — sending money, deleting files, emailing someone — needs more than good intentions to be safe to run unsupervised.

agents/autonomy-levels-and-human-oversig.title: Autonomy Levels and Human Oversight Tiers
agents/autonomy-levels-and-human-oversig.path: Agents/Agent Safety and Governance/Autonomy Levels and Human Oversight Tiers.md
agents/autonomy-levels-and-human-oversig.summary: An agent that must stop and ask before every single action is safe but slow; an agent that never asks is fast but unwatched.

glossary.def: every action requires a person's approval before it runs.
the agent runs autonomously, but irreversible actions are routed through a person first.
the agent acts fully autonomously, with no approval step at all.

agents/sandboxing-and-isolation.title: Sandboxing and Isolation
agents/sandboxing-and-isolation.path: Agents/Agent Safety and Governance/Sandboxing and Isolation.md
agents/sandboxing-and-isolation.summary: A code-execution agent running generated code with full access to the host machine can reach every file on it — including ones that have nothing to do with its task.

glossary.def: an isolated execution environment that restricts what a running process can reach.
how much damage a mistake or attack can cause, bounded by what it can actually reach.
containing a process so its effects can't spread beyond an intended boundary.

agents/excessive-agency-and-scope-limits.title: Excessive Agency and Scope Limits
agents/excessive-agency-and-scope-limits.path: Agents/Agent Safety and Governance/Excessive Agency and Scope Limits.md
agents/excessive-agency-and-scope-limits.summary: An agent built to summarize an inbox only needs to read email.

glossary.def: granting an agent tools, permissions, or autonomy beyond what its task requires.
granting only the tools a task genuinely needs, nothing more.
the actions an attempted manipulation can actually carry out, limited by which tools were granted.

agents/guardrails-for-agent-actions.title: Guardrails for Agent Actions
agents/guardrails-for-agent-actions.path: Agents/Agent Safety and Governance/Guardrails for Agent Actions.md
agents/guardrails-for-agent-actions.summary: A text guardrail scores free-form output for risk and has to guess at intent from wording alone.

glossary.def: a check that matches a proposed action's structured parameters against a policy before it executes.
a rule identifying action parameters (a command, a table, an amount) that should be blocked or flagged.
the specific, checkable fields of a proposed action, as opposed to unstructured free text.

agents/prompt-injection-in-agent-context.title: Prompt Injection in Agent Contexts
agents/prompt-injection-in-agent-context.path: Agents/Agent Safety and Governance/Prompt Injection in Agent Contexts.md
agents/prompt-injection-in-agent-context.summary: A chatbot tricked by hidden text into saying something it shouldn't is embarrassing.

glossary.def: text crafted to look like an instruction, embedded in content a model reads, attempting to redirect its behavior.
a real action an agent takes as a result of following an injected instruction rather than its actual task.
restricting which actions are available at all, so an injected instruction has nothing exploitable to request.

agents/agents-in-practice.title: Agents in Practice
agents/agents-in-practice.summary: Everything on this road so far has covered one piece of an agent at a time.

agents/observability-and-tracing-for-age.title: Observability and Tracing for Agent Runs
agents/observability-and-tracing-for-age.path: Agents/Agents in Practice/Observability and Tracing for Agent Runs.md
agents/observability-and-tracing-for-age.summary: When an agent's final answer is wrong, the final answer alone almost never says why.

glossary.def: the ability to inspect what actually happened during a run after it finishes.
recording each step of a run as its own span, capturing its tool, input, output, latency and cost.
one recorded unit of a trace — typically one step's full record.

agents/production-agent-architecture.title: Production Agent Architecture
agents/production-agent-architecture.summary: Every topic on this road so far has zoomed into one piece of an agent — planning, a tool call, a memory lookup.

glossary.def: the repeating observe-reason-act-verify cycle a running agent executes each iteration.
the LLM call deciding what to do next, typically the loop's dominant latency cost.
how a loop iteration's total latency divides among its constituent stages.

agents/cost-and-latency-of-agent-loops.title: Cost and Latency of Agent Loops
agents/cost-and-latency-of-agent-loops.path: Agents/Agents in Practice/Cost and Latency of Agent Loops.md
agents/cost-and-latency-of-agent-loops.summary: A single LLM call's cost and latency already has its own math, covered on the LLMs planet.

glossary.def: a loop's total cost growing faster than linearly because each iteration's own cost is higher than the last.
the accumulated history an agent's reasoning call includes with every new iteration.
the (inaccurate) assumption that every iteration of a loop costs the same as the first one.

agents/capstone-a-goal-decomposed-execut.title: Capstone: A Goal, Decomposed, Executed and Verified End to End
agents/capstone-a-goal-decomposed-execut.path: Agents/Agents in Practice/Capstone: A Goal, Decomposed, Executed and Verified End to End.md
agents/capstone-a-goal-decomposed-execut.summary: Every mechanism this planet covered separately — decomposing a goal, picking a tool, sharing state across steps, checking a trajectory, gating a risky action, accounting for cost — is usually…

glossary.def: following one goal through every stage of a pipeline in order, rather than examining each stage in isolation.
a sequence of subtasks where every task runs only after everything it depends on has already completed.
which category of an agent's actions require a human's approval before running, scoped specifically to irreversible or high-risk ones.
